name: Lemon Butter Baked Cod and Rice
instructions:
Rinse the rice if your package suggests it, then bring it to a boil with about 2 cups water for every 1 cup rice; cover, reduce to low, and cook until tender so it finishes near the cod.
Heat the oven to 425F and lightly grease a baking dish.
Arrange the cod in the dish, top it with lemon slices, butter, garlic if using, and pepper if using, then keep the pieces in one layer so they bake evenly.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the cod turns opaque and flakes easily in the center.
Spoon the cod over the rice, drizzle the lemony pan juices over each serving, and serve hot with extra lemon from the dish.

name: Baked Ravioli with Sausage
instructions: Brown the sausage in a skillet over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes until well browned. If using onion, cook it with the sausage over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until softened. Stir in marinara and let it bubble for 1 minute. Layer the ravioli with the sauce plus mozzarella and parmesan if using in a baking dish so the pasta stays coated. Bake at 375F for 20 to 25 minutes until the ravioli is tender and the top is browned in spots.

name: BBQ Beef Biscuit Bake
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and lightly grease a baking dish.
Brown the beef over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the meat is fully browned. If using onion, cook it with the beef until softened.
Stir in the BBQ sauce and corn if using, then simmer for 2 minutes until the filling looks thick and glossy.
Spoon the filling into the baking dish, top with pieces of biscuit dough and cheddar if using, and bake for 14 to 16 minutes until the biscuits are golden and the filling bubbles around the edges.

name: BBQ Chicken Biscuit Bake
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and lightly grease a baking dish.
Cook the chicken over medium-high heat for 5 to 7 minutes until the pieces are browned and no longer pink in the center. If using onion, cook it with the chicken until softened.
Stir in the BBQ sauce and corn if using, then simmer for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to coat the chicken.
Transfer the mixture to the baking dish, top with pieces of biscuit dough and cheddar if using, and bake for 14 to 16 minutes until the biscuits are browned and the sauce bubbles.

name: Beef and Potato Tacos
instructions:
Boil the potato pieces in a small pot of water or microwave them with a splash of water for 4 to 5 minutes until they start to soften.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pan is dry.
Cook the ground beef with the potato for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until the beef has no pink remaining and the potato is tender with crisp edges.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for 30 to 60 seconds per side so they stay flexible, or cook a little longer if you want crisp edges.
Fill the tortillas with the beef and potato mixture, then top with onion, salsa, or cheddar if using and serve while hot.

name: Beef Pasta Bake
instructions:
Heat the oven to 375F and lightly grease a baking dish.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta 1 to 2 minutes shy of tender, then drain it so it can finish in the bake.
While the pasta cooks, heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the ground beef for 6 to 8 minutes until no pink remains. If using onion, cook it with the beef until softened; if using garlic, stir it in for the last 30 seconds so it does not burn.
Stir in the tomato sauce, fold in the drained pasta, and spread everything evenly in the baking dish so the pasta is coated.
Top with mozzarella if using, then bake for 18 to 22 minutes until the edges bubble and the cheese is melted with browned spots or the top is hot, then rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Sesame Soy Beef Noodles
instructions:
Bring a medium pot of water to a boil and cook the ramen for 2 to 3 minutes just until loosened, then drain well so it stir-fries instead of steaming.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pan is dry.
Cook the beef for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it into bite-size pieces, until browned and cooked through.
Add cabbage and garlic if using and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the cabbage wilts but still has a little bite; lower the heat if the garlic starts to brown too fast.
Add the noodles and soy sauce, toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until glossy, then top with green onion if using and serve hot.

name: Beef Sloppy Joes
instructions:
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat, add the ground beef and onion if using, and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until the beef is browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the tomato paste with 1/2 cup water, mustard, and brown sugar if using, then simmer over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes until thick and glossy.
Toast the bread for 1 to 2 minutes so it can hold the saucy beef.
Spoon the sloppy joe filling onto the bread and serve hot while the sauce is thick enough to mound.

name: Creamy Beef Stroganoff Skillet Noodles
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles until just tender. While the noodles cook, heat a large skillet over high heat, sear the steak strips in a little oil for 1 to 2 minutes per side until browned but still slightly pink in the center, then transfer to a plate. Reduce the heat to medium and cook the mushrooms for 5 minutes until browned. If using onion, cook it with the mushrooms until softened; if using garlic, stir it in for 30 seconds. Add the cream and a splash of noodle water and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes until lightly thickened. Return the steak and any juices to the skillet, toss with the drained noodles for 1 minute, and serve when the sauce coats the noodles and the steak is just cooked through.

name: Homestyle Beef Vegetable Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pot is dry.
Brown the beef for 6 to 8 minutes until the meat has no pink remaining; drain excess fat if needed. If using onion, cook it with the beef until softened.
Stir in diced tomatoes if using, then add about 5 cups beef broth if using; otherwise add about 5 cups water. Bring the pot to a steady simmer.
Add the potatoes and carrots, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 15 to 18 minutes until both are tender when pierced with a fork.
Stir in green beans if using for the last 3 minutes so they stay bright, then taste for salt and ladle the soup while hot.

name: Black Bean Enchilada Skillet
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium heat with a small splash of oil if the pan is dry.
If using onion, cook it for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened.
Stir in the enchilada sauce and black beans. If using corn, add it now. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until the mixture is bubbling and hot.
Tear the corn tortillas into strips and fold them into the sauce. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the strips soften but still hold some shape.
If using cheddar, sprinkle it over the top, cover the skillet for 1 minute, and let it melt. Serve hot.

name: Black Bean Tacos
instructions:
Heat a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Add the black beans and salsa if using, then simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until the beans are hot and thick enough to spoon. Mash a few beans into the pan so the filling holds together.
Warm and flip the tortillas in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side so they stay flexible.
Fold the bean filling into the tortillas. Top with cheddar, extra salsa, or lime if using, and serve while the filling is still steamy.

name: Paprika Catfish Corn Skillet
instructions:
Pat the catfish dry and season it with paprika, salt, and pepper if using.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat, then sear the catfish for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and the fish flakes easily.
Move the catfish to a plate, add the corn and onion to the skillet, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the corn blisters and the onion softens.
Return the catfish for 1 minute to warm through, then finish with lemon if using and serve hot.

name: Cheesy Baked Ziti
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Cook the ziti 2 minutes shy of package directions so it finishes in the oven instead of turning soft.
Warm the marinara in a saucepan with the garlic and Italian seasoning if using, then simmer it over medium-low heat for 2 minutes until it loosens and smells rich.
Fold the drained ziti into the sauce with half the mozzarella, half the parmesan, and the ricotta if using so the pasta stays saucy all the way through.
Transfer the pasta to a baking dish, spread it into an even layer, and top with the remaining mozzarella and parmesan so the cheese browns evenly in the oven.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the sauce bubbles around the edges and the top is browned in spots, then rest for 5 minutes so each scoop holds together with cheesy strands instead of sliding apart.

name: Cheesy Beef Taco Skillet
instructions:
Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat and add the ground beef.
Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until browned with no pink remaining; spoon off excess fat if the pan looks greasy.
Stir in the onion and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until it softens, then add salsa if using and scrape the browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Fold in the torn tortillas and cook for 1 to 2 minutes so some pieces soften in the sauce while a few edges stay chewy.
Reduce the heat to low, scatter the cheddar over the top, cover for 1 minute until melted, and serve with lettuce if using.

name: Garlic Alfredo Chicken Pasta
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until just shy of tender. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
While the pasta cooks, heat a skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil if the pan is dry.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring a few times, until lightly golden and no longer pink in the center.
Lower the heat to medium. Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
Pour in the cream and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Add the drained pasta and parmesan. Toss for 1 minute, adding a splash of pasta water if needed, until the noodles are coated and the sauce is silky. Finish with pepper if using.

name: Chicken and Dumpling Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat with butter if using, or use a small splash of oil if the pot is dry.
Add the chicken and carrot. If using onion or celery, add them now. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables start to soften and the chicken loses its raw color.
Pour in about 4 cups chicken broth if using, or use water. Bring the pot to a gentle simmer.
Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until the chicken is tender and no pink remains in the center.
In a small bowl, mix the flour with a few tablespoons of water or broth until it forms a thick, spoonable dumpling batter.
Drop small spoonfuls of batter over the simmering soup. Cover loosely and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, until the dumplings are puffed and no longer doughy in the center.
Taste for salt if needed and serve hot.

name: Chicken Bacon Pasta Bake
instructions:
Heat the oven to 375F and lightly grease a baking dish.
Cook the pasta until just shy of tender, then drain it well so it can finish in the oven.
While the pasta cooks, crisp the bacon in a skillet. Transfer the bacon to a plate, leaving a small amount of fat in the pan if useful.
Add the chicken to the skillet and cook over medium-high heat for 5 to 7 minutes, until lightly browned and no longer pink in the center. If using onion, cook it with the chicken until softened.
In the baking dish, toss the cooked pasta with the chicken mixture and cream if using. If using cheddar, stir in half now so the pasta stays coated.
Top with the bacon. If using cheddar, scatter the remaining cheddar over the top.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the edges bubble and the top is hot. If cheddar is used, bake until the cheese is melted.

name: Salsa Verde Chicken Burrito Bowl
instructions:
Cook the rice according to the package directions, or simmer about 1 cup rice with 2 cups water for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pan is dry.
Cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned at the edges and no pink remains in the center.
Stir in the salsa verde and black beans, then simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until the beans are hot and the sauce lightly coats the chicken; lower the heat if it bubbles hard.
Spoon the rice into bowls and top with the saucy chicken mixture. Add corn, cheddar, or cilantro if using, and serve hot.

name: Chicken Cabbage Stir Fry
instructions:
Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat with 1 tablespoon oil.
Cook the chicken for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pieces are browned and no pink remains in the center.
Add the cabbage. If using carrot, add it now. Stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until the vegetables soften but still have some crunch.
If using garlic, stir it in for 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce and cook for 1 minute, tossing until everything looks glossy.
Serve right away on its own or over rice if using, before the cabbage loses its crunch.

name: Chicken Enchilada Rice Skillet
instructions:
Heat a deep skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil if the pan is dry.
Cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, until lightly browned on the outside. If using onion, cook it with the chicken until softened.
Stir in the rice, enchilada sauce, black beans if using, and 2 cups water, scraping the bottom so the rice is evenly covered.
Bring the pan to a boil, then cover and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 16 to 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165F or has no pink in the center.
Top with cheddar if using, cover for 1 minute until melted, and rest off the heat for 3 minutes before serving.

name: Chicken Florentine Pasta
instructions:
Fill a large pot about 2/3 full with water, salt it lightly, and bring it to a boil.
Cook the pasta until just tender, stirring once after adding it. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
While the pasta cooks, heat a deep skillet over medium-high heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pan is dry. Cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, until browned and no pink remains in the center.
If using garlic, stir it in for the last 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the spinach and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until wilted.
If using cream, stir it in and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, until it lightly coats a spoon.
Toss in the pasta and parmesan if using, adding a splash of pasta water if the pan looks dry. Serve while glossy.

name: Classic Chicken Noodle Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat with a small splash of oil if the pot is dry.
Add the carrot. If using onion or celery, add them now. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are glossy and starting to soften.
Add the chicken and about 5 cups chicken broth if using, or use water. Bring the pot to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 12 to 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165F or has no pink in the center. Shred or chop the chicken in the pot.
Add the noodles and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes, until just tender.
Finish with parsley if using and serve hot before the noodles soak up too much broth.

name: Mozzarella Chicken Parmesan Bake
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and lightly grease a baking dish; this takes about 1 minute.
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce in the dish, then arrange the chicken breast in one even layer so the pieces brown at the same pace.
Season with Italian seasoning if using, then spoon the remaining tomato sauce over the chicken so each piece is covered.
Scatter mozzarella and parmesan over the top so the cheese melts evenly.
Bake for 22 to 24 minutes, until the thickest piece reaches 165F and the cheese is browned and bubbling at the edges.
Rest for 3 minutes, then serve with pasta if using or spoon the extra sauce from the dish over the chicken.

name: Creamy Chicken Pot Pie Skillet
instructions:
Heat a deep skillet over medium-high heat with a light film of oil.
Add the chicken and carrot. If using onion, add it now. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is lightly browned and no longer pink in the center and the carrot starts to soften.
Reduce the heat to medium. Stir in the peas and cream, scraping the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Nestle pieces of biscuit dough on top, cover, and cook over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until the filling is bubbling and the dough is dry in the center instead of sticky.
Let the skillet rest for 2 minutes before serving.

name: Chicken Ramen Stir Fry
instructions:
Bring a pot of water to a boil over high heat. Cook the ramen for 2 to 3 minutes, just until loosened, then drain well so the noodles stir-fry instead of steam.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil if the pan is dry.
Cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and no pink remains in the center.
If using cabbage, carrot, or green onion, add them now and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until just tender.
Add the noodles and soy sauce. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, tossing until hot, glossy, and lightly caramelized around the edges.

name: Chicken Stuffing Bake
instructions:
Heat the oven to 375F and lightly grease a baking dish.
Prepare the stuffing mix according to the package directions, or moisten it with hot water until soft but not soupy.
Spread the chicken in an even layer in the baking dish. If using onion or green beans, scatter them with the chicken.
Spoon the cream over the chicken mixture so the base stays moist.
Scatter the stuffing evenly over the top. If using cheddar, sprinkle it over the stuffing or under the stuffing layer.
Cover loosely with foil and bake for 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165F or has no pink in the center.
Uncover and bake for 8 to 10 minutes more, until the topping is crisp and browned at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Chicken Taco Rice Skillet
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium heat with a small splash of oil if the pan is dry.
Cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until lightly browned on the outside. If using onion, cook it with the chicken until softened.
Stir in the rice, salsa, and 2 cups water, then bring the pan to a boil over high heat.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165F or has no pink in the center.
Toast the tortilla strips in a dry skillet for 1 to 2 minutes, until crisp at the edges.
Fold some tortilla strips into the rice, then top with cheddar if using and the remaining tortilla strips before serving.

name: Chicken Tortilla Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat with a small splash of oil if the pot is dry.
Cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, until lightly browned and no longer raw on the outside. If using onion, cook it with the chicken until softened.
Stir in the tomato sauce and about 4 cups chicken broth if using, or use water. Bring the pot to a gentle boil.
Reduce to a simmer and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165F or is tender with no pink in the center.
Stir in the tortilla strips. If using beans or corn, add them now. Simmer for 2 minutes, until some tortilla strips soften into the broth while others keep a little chew.
Serve hot with extra tortilla strips on top if you saved any.

name: Chickpea Potato Curry
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pot is dry.
If using onion, cook it for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the potato, chickpeas, tomato sauce if using, and enough water to barely cover. Scrape the bottom so the spices do not stick.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to medium-low. Simmer for 16 to 18 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the potatoes are tender.
If using spinach, stir it in for 1 to 2 minutes, until wilted.
Simmer uncovered for 2 minutes more if the curry looks thin, or add 1 to 2 tablespoons water if it looks dry. Serve hot.

name: Chili Mac Skillet
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until just tender. Reserve 1/4 cup pasta water, then drain.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the ground beef for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink remaining. If using onion, cook it with the beef until softened.
Stir in the beans, tomato sauce, and reserved pasta water. Simmer over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Fold in the pasta. If using cheddar, stir it in and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until melted and the sauce clings to the noodles.
Serve hot.

name: Creamy Stovetop Mac and Cheese
instructions:
Bring a medium pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta until tender but not mushy, then drain it well.
While the pasta cooks, warm the milk in a saucepan over medium-low heat. If using butter, add it now. Keep the milk steaming but not boiling hard.
Stir in the cheddar a handful at a time until melted and smooth, lowering the heat if it starts to bubble hard or look grainy.
Fold the pasta into the sauce and cook for 1 minute, until every piece is coated.
Season with pepper or mustard if using, then serve within 1 minute while the sauce is silky and creamy.

name: Coconut Chicken Curry
instructions:
Heat a pot or deep skillet over medium heat with a small splash of oil if the pan is dry.
Cook the onion for 4 to 5 minutes, until softened and glossy.
Stir in the curry powder for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until the chicken turns opaque on the outside.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring it to a gentle boil, and lower the heat if it bubbles hard.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165F or has no pink in the center and the sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in spinach if using for 1 minute, until wilted. Serve on its own or over rice if using.

name: Coconut Ginger Chickpea Curry
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pot is dry.
Cook the onion and ginger for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened and fragrant. If using curry powder, stir it in for the last 30 seconds.
Stir in the chickpeas, coconut milk, and tomato sauce if using, scraping the bottom so the ginger does not stick.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Fold in spinach if using for 1 to 2 minutes, until wilted. Serve hot.

name: Coconut Tomato Lentil Curry
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pot is dry.
Cook the onion for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened and fragrant.
Stir in the curry powder for 1 minute, until it smells toasted.
Add the lentils, coconut milk, tomato sauce, and enough water to cover the lentils by about 1 inch, then bring the pot to a boil.
Reduce to medium-low. Cook for 20 to 24 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and the curry is thick.
Add 1 to 2 tablespoons water if it starts sticking. If using spinach, stir it in for 2 to 3 minutes, until wilted. Serve hot.

name: Creamy Tomato Beef Shells
instructions:
Fill a large pot about 2/3 full with water, add a good pinch of salt, and bring it to a boil.
Cook the shells until just shy of tender, stirring once after adding them so they do not stick. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
While the pasta cooks, heat a deep skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the beef for 6 to 8 minutes, until no pink remains. If using onion, cook it with the beef until softened. Drain if the pan looks greasy.
Reduce the heat to medium. Stir in the tomato sauce and cream. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until the sauce looks smooth and coats a spoon.
Fold in the shells and cheddar if using, adding a splash of pasta water if the pan looks dry. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until glossy before serving.

name: Cozy Creamy Chicken Rice Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pot is dry.
Add the carrot. If using onion or celery, add them now. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and glossy.
Add the chicken, rice, and about 5 cups water. Bring the pot to a gentle simmer.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 16 to 18 minutes, stirring once or twice so the rice does not stick, until the rice is tender and the chicken has no pink in the center.
Stir in the cream and simmer for 1 minute more without boiling hard.
Serve while the broth is silky.

name: Creamy Sausage Pasta
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until just tender, then reserve 1/2 cup pasta water and drain.
While the pasta cooks, heat a deep skillet over medium-high heat and brown the sausage for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into small pieces until no pink remains.
Stir in the garlic if using for 30 seconds, then lower the heat to medium and pour in the cream.
Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce lightly coats a spoon, adding a splash of pasta water if it gets too thick.
Toss in the drained pasta, spinach if using, and parmesan if using for 1 to 2 minutes until the pasta is glossy and the spinach wilts.

name: Creamy Tomato Beef Pasta
instructions:
Fill a large pot about 2/3 full with water, add a good pinch of salt, and bring it to a boil.
Cook the pasta for 8 to 10 minutes, until just shy of tender, stirring once so it does not stick. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
While the pasta cooks, heat a deep skillet over medium-high heat and cook the ground beef for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until fully browned with no pink remaining.
If using garlic, stir it in for 1 minute.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and pour in the cream and tomato sauce.
Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until the sauce turns glossy and coats a spoon, lowering the heat if it bubbles hard.
Add the pasta and parmesan if using. Toss for 1 minute, loosening with a splash of pasta water if needed before serving.

name: Crispy Bean Tostadas
instructions:
Heat the oven to 425F and arrange the tortillas on a sheet pan in one layer; this setup takes about 1 minute.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until crisp and sturdy enough to hold toppings.
While the tortillas crisp, warm the beans in a skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until hot and spreadable; add 1 to 2 tablespoons water if they look dry.
Spread the beans over each tostada shell, sprinkle with cheddar, and bake for 2 to 3 minutes until the cheese melts.
Top with lettuce, salsa, and lime if using, then serve within 1 to 2 minutes while the shells stay crisp.

name: Crispy Soy Salmon Rice Bowl
instructions:
Cook the rice first according to the package directions so it can stay covered and warm while the salmon cooks.
Pat the salmon dry so it sears instead of steaming, then heat a skillet over medium-high heat with 1 tablespoon oil if needed.
Cook the salmon for 3 to 4 minutes on the first side and 2 to 3 minutes on the second until the outside is crisp and the center is opaque and flakes easily.
Drizzle the soy sauce into the pan during the last minute so it lightly glazes the fish without burning.
Rest the salmon for 1 minute, break it into large pieces, and serve over rice with cucumber, avocado, and green onion if using.

name: Scallion Egg Fried Noodles
instructions:
Bring a medium pot of water to a boil and cook the noodles for 3 to 5 minutes, until just tender. Drain well so they fry instead of steam.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pan is dry.
If using onion or carrot, cook them for 2 to 3 minutes, until crisp-tender, then push them to one side.
Add the egg to the open side and scramble for 1 to 2 minutes, until softly set.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, and green onion. Toss for 2 to 3 minutes, until hot and lightly browned in spots, then serve right away.

name: Garlic Broccoli Soy Noodles
instructions:
Fill a medium pot about 2/3 full with water and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Cook the ramen for 2 minutes, then add the broccoli for the last 2 minutes so the noodles loosen and the broccoli turns bright green.
Drain well, leaving only 1 to 2 tablespoons water in the pot so the noodles stay saucy but not soupy.
Return the pot to medium heat. Add soy sauce and garlic, then toss for 1 minute, until the noodles are coated and the garlic smells fragrant.
Top with egg or green onion if using, and serve right away while the broccoli still has a little bite.

name: Lemon Garlic Butter Tilapia Skillet
instructions:
Pat the tilapia dry while a skillet heats over medium-high heat so the fish sears instead of steaming.
Heat the skillet with the butter, then cook the fillets for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until lightly golden and flaky in the center.
Add the garlic for the final minute so it turns fragrant without burning.
Squeeze in the lemon and spoon the lemon-garlic butter from the pan over the fish before serving. Finish with pepper or parsley if using.

name: Garlic Chicken and Green Beans
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and sear the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring once or twice, until browned and no pink remains on the thickest pieces.
Add the green beans and garlic and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the beans are crisp-tender and the garlic smells fragrant.
Toss in soy sauce or a squeeze of lemon for the last 30 seconds until the chicken looks glossy, then serve right away.

name: Ground Beef Quesadillas
instructions:
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the ground beef for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until fully browned with no pink remaining. If using onion or bell pepper, cook them with the beef until softened.
Transfer the filling to a bowl and wipe out the skillet if the pan looks greasy.
Lay cheddar and a thin layer of beef filling over half of each flour tortilla, then fold the tortillas closed.
Return the quesadillas to the skillet over medium heat. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until the tortillas are crisp and browned in spots and the cheese is melted.
Slice into wedges and serve with salsa if using.

name: Lemon Garlic Chicken and Chickpeas
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil.
Cook the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through to 165F. Transfer it to a plate.
Add the garlic and chickpeas to the skillet. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until the chickpeas are hot and starting to crisp at the edges.
Return the chicken to the pan. If using tomato, add it now and cook for 1 minute.
If using spinach, fold it in just until wilted.
Finish with the lemon juice, toss to coat everything, and serve while the chicken is juicy and the chickpeas are bright and lemony.

name: Lemon Garlic Chicken Rice Bowl
instructions:
Cook the rice according to the package directions, or simmer 1 cup rice with about 2 cups water until tender. Keep it covered while the chicken cooks.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pan is dry.
Cook the chicken with the garlic for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and no pink remains in the center.
Lower the heat to medium, fold in the lemon juice, and cook for 30 seconds, until the chicken looks glossy.
Build bowls with rice and chicken. Add cucumber, tomato, or olives if using, and serve while the chicken is warm and the rice is fluffy.

name: Roasted Lemon Garlic Salmon
instructions:
Heat the oven to 425F and lightly oil a sheet pan with olive oil if using.
Set the salmon on the pan in one layer and season it with garlic, lemon, and pepper if using.
Roast for 12 to 14 minutes, until the thickest part flakes easily with a fork and the center is just opaque but still moist.
Rest the salmon for 1 minute so the juices settle.
Spoon the lemony pan juices over the top and finish with parsley if using.

name: Lemon Chicken Potato Sheet Pan
instructions:
Heat the oven to 425F and line or lightly grease a sheet pan.
Cut the potatoes into small even pieces. Toss them with the chicken, lemon, garlic if using, and a small splash of oil if needed.
Spread everything in one layer so the chicken roasts instead of steaming.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring the potatoes once, until the chicken reaches 165F and the potatoes are browned and tender when pierced with a fork.
If using zucchini or onion, add them for the last 12 to 15 minutes. Serve hot with extra lemon from the pan spooned over the top.

name: Lentil Spinach Curry
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat and cook the onion with a drizzle of oil for 4 to 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lentils, tomato sauce, and 3 cups water and bring the pot to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the lentils are tender and the curry thickens.
Stir in the spinach and coconut milk if using and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the spinach wilts, then serve hot.

name: Lentil Tomato Stew
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat and cook the onion with the carrot and garlic, if using, for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the lentils, diced tomatoes, cumin if using, and 3 cups water and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes until the lentils are tender and the stew thickens.
Add a splash of water if the pot looks dry and simmer 1 minute more before serving.
Taste for salt and keep the stew at a low bubble until it is hot all the way through.

name: Cheddar Broccoli Loaded Baked Potatoes
instructions:
Heat the oven to 425F and bake the potatoes directly on the rack or on a sheet pan for 40 to 50 minutes until a knife slides easily through the center.
While the potatoes bake, cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until browned and crisp, then drain on a paper towel and crumble.
Split each hot potato open, fluff the center with a fork, and fill with cheddar and bacon so the cheese melts into the potato.
Top with sour cream, green onion, and black pepper if using, then serve right away.

name: Loaded Cheddar Chicken Potato Casserole
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and lightly grease a baking dish.
Microwave or simmer the potatoes for 8 to 10 minutes until they start to soften.
Toss the potatoes with the chicken, cream if using, and half of the cheddar until everything is evenly coated.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the potatoes are tender and the thickest pieces of chicken reach 165F with no pink in the center.
Sprinkle the bacon, green onion, and remaining cheddar over the top and bake 5 minutes more until the cheese is melted, then rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Mediterranean Chickpea Skillet
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pan is dry.
Cook the onion for 4 to 5 minutes until softened and glossy.
Add garlic if using and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add tomato sauce and chickpeas.
Bring the skillet to a simmer, reduce to medium-low, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the chickpeas.
Fold in spinach if using for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted, then finish with lemon if using and serve hot while the sauce is glossy.

name: Mexican Bean and Corn Rice Skillet
instructions:
Heat a deep skillet over medium heat with 1 tablespoon oil.
Add onion if using and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until softened, then stir in the rice for 1 minute so the grains turn glossy.
Add the beans, corn, tomato sauce if using, and 2 cups water, scraping the bottom so nothing sticks.
Bring the skillet to a steady simmer, cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 16 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Turn off the heat, sprinkle cheddar over the top if using, cover for 1 minute to melt, and rest 3 minutes before serving.

name: Minestrone Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat with 1 tablespoon oil if the pot is dry.
Cook carrot and celery if using for 4 to 5 minutes until they start to soften.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes with 4 cups vegetable broth if using, or water, and bring to a boil.
Add the beans, reduce the heat to a gentle simmer, and cook for 10 minutes so the broth starts to taste rich.
Stir in the pasta and zucchini if using and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the pasta is tender but not mushy; taste for salt and serve hot with parmesan if using.

name: One Pot Sausage Marinara Pasta
instructions: Heat a deep pot over medium-high heat and cook the sausage with the onion for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking the meat into small pieces, until the sausage is browned and hot through. Stir in the garlic and cook over medium heat for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the marinara, dry pasta, plus enough water to just cover the noodles and bring the pot to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the pasta is tender and the sauce thickens enough to cling to the noodles. Fold in the spinach for the last 1 to 2 minutes until just wilted, then serve while the sauce is still glossy.

name: Crispy Lemon Pan-Fried Bass
instructions:
Pat the bass dry and season it with salt and pepper so the surface can brown properly.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat until the oil shimmers.
Sear the fish for 3 to 4 minutes on the first side until deeply golden at the edges.
Flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, then finish with lemon and garlic if using.

name: Pesto Chicken Pasta
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until just shy of tender while you heat a skillet with a little oil over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, season with black pepper, and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pieces are golden and cooked through with no pink in the center. Lower the heat to medium and toss the hot pasta with the pesto so the noodles are evenly coated. Fold the pesto pasta into the skillet with the chicken, then stir in the spinach or tomato for 1 to 2 minutes until the greens wilt or the tomatoes warm through. Finish with parmesan and serve while the pasta is glossy and hot.

name: Garlic Ginger Pork Stir-Fry
instructions:
Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork for 4 to 5 minutes until browned and no longer pink in the center.
Add the bell pepper and onion and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds until fragrant, then toss in the soy sauce until the pork is coated and the sauce looks glossy.
Serve right away with rice if you want a fuller meal.

name: Roasted Veggie Pasta
instructions:
Heat the oven to 425F and spread the bell pepper and zucchini on a sheet pan in one layer with 1 tablespoon oil if you have it.
Roast for 18 to 20 minutes until tender and browned at the edges, stirring once halfway through.
While the vegetables roast, fill a large pot about 2/3 full with water, salt it lightly, and cook the pasta until just tender; reserve 1/2 cup pasta water and drain.
Warm garlic and tomato sauce if using in the pot over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce loosens.
Toss in the pasta, roasted vegetables, and parmesan if using, adding a splash of pasta water if dry.
Serve right away while the vegetables still have browned edges and the pasta is steaming.

name: Sausage Bean Chili
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat and cook the sausage with the onion, if using, for 6 to 8 minutes until browned and no pink remains.
Stir for 1 minute to break the sausage into small pieces so the chili stays spoonable.
Stir in the beans, tomato sauce, and 1 cup water and bring the chili to a low simmer.
Cook uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chili thickens and the beans are heated through.
Top the bowls with cheddar if using and let it melt for 1 minute before serving hot.

name: Sausage Pepper Skillet
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium heat and cook the sausage for 6 to 8 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through.
If needed, move the sausage to a plate, then cook the peppers and onion in the rendered fat for 4 to 5 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Return the sausage to the skillet, add garlic if using, and cook for 1 minute until the garlic is fragrant and everything is hot.

name: Sausage Tortellini Soup
instructions: Heat a soup pot over medium heat and brown the sausage with onion for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until the sausage is fully cooked and the onion is softened. Add the tomato sauce and water and bring the broth to a gentle boil over medium-high heat. Stir in the tortellini and spinach and simmer for 4 to 6 minutes until the pasta is tender, then add a splash of cream if using and serve.

name: Chile Lime Bean Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a saucepan over medium heat with a splash of oil, then cook the onion for 3 to 4 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Stir in the beans with a splash of water and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until hot, saucy, and lightly thickened.
Spoon the beans over the rice, finish with lime, cilantro, or hot sauce if using, and serve while the bowls are warm.

name: Shrimp Garlic Noodles
instructions:
Fill a medium pot about 2/3 full with water and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Cook the noodles until just tender, then reserve 1/2 cup cooking water and drain well so they do not turn watery in the skillet.
Pat the shrimp dry, heat 1 tablespoon oil or butter if using in a large skillet over medium-high heat, and cook the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes per side until pink, opaque, and curled.
Add the garlic during the last 30 seconds so it smells fragrant but does not burn.
Add the noodles back to the skillet with a splash of cooking water and toss for 1 minute until glossy; finish with butter, lemon, or pepper if using and serve right away while the shrimp are still tender.

name: Skillet Chicken Ginger Rice
instructions:
Heat a deep skillet over medium heat with the oil if using.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook over medium heat for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 4 to 6 minutes until the pieces are lightly browned and cooked through with no pink remaining.
Toss in the rice and soy sauce until the grains are coated.
Pour in 2 cups of water and bring the pan to a low boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest the skillet off the heat for 5 minutes, fluff the rice, and add onion or pepper on top if you want extra crunch.

name: Skillet Chicken Parmesan Pasta
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until just shy of tender while you start the sauce.
Heat a deep skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil.
Season the chicken with salt, pepper, and italian seasoning if using, then cook for 5 to 7 minutes until the pieces are browned in spots and cooked through to 165F.
Add the garlic if using, stir for 30 seconds, then pour in the tomato sauce and simmer for 2 minutes so the chicken is coated in a thick red sauce.
Stir in the drained pasta with a splash of pasta water and half of the parmesan until the sauce clings to the noodles.
Scatter the mozzarella and remaining parmesan over the skillet, cover on low for 1 to 2 minutes until the cheese melts into a chicken-parmesan-style top, and serve while the pasta is saucy and the cheese is still stretchy.

name: Skillet Lasagna Pasta
instructions: Heat a deep skillet over medium-high heat and cook the ground beef with the onion for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until the beef is richly browned and no pink remains. Stir in the tomato sauce plus a splash of water and bring the skillet to a boil. Add the pasta and cover the skillet. Cook over medium-low heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the noodles are tender and the sauce thickens enough to cling to them. Scatter mozzarella and parmesan over the top, cover for 1 minute on low heat until the cheese melts, then serve straight from the skillet.

name: Soy Scallion Egg Ramen
instructions:
Bring the chicken broth to a boil over high heat, then add the ramen and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until springy but not mushy.
Simmer the egg in the same pot or a second pan over medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes for a soft center, then peel and halve it.
Stir soy sauce and sesame oil if using into the hot broth, then add spinach if using and simmer for 1 minute until wilted.
Top the ramen soup with the egg and green onion, and serve while the noodles are still springy.

name: Soy Sesame Tofu Rice Bowl
instructions:
Cook the rice first and let it steam, covered, for 5 minutes while you finish the tofu.
Pat the tofu dry, cut it into cubes, and toss it with a spoonful of soy sauce.
Cook the tofu in a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the edges are browned and crisp.
Stir in the remaining soy sauce with 2 tablespoons water and cook for 1 minute until the tofu is glazed.
Build bowls with the rice, tofu, and cucumber, carrot, and green onion if using, then serve right away while the tofu stays hot.

name: Spinach Ricotta Pasta Bake
instructions:
Heat the oven to 375F and lightly grease a baking dish.
Fill a large pot about 2/3 full with water, salt it lightly, and cook the pasta 1 to 2 minutes shy of tender so it finishes in the oven.
Drain the pasta, then stir it with ricotta, tomato sauce, spinach if using, and garlic if using until the noodles are evenly coated.
Spread the mixture in the baking dish and top with mozzarella and parmesan if using.
Bake for 20 to 24 minutes until the center is hot, the edges bubble, and the top is browned in patches.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving so each scoop holds together.

name: Sweet Potato Black Bean Hash
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium heat and cook the sweet potato and onion for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the cubes are tender and browned at the edges. Fold in the black beans, cumin, salt, and pepper and cook for 2 minutes until the beans are heated through. Top with a fried egg if using and serve with hot sauce.

name: Tofu Veggie Stir Fry
instructions:
Press the tofu dry, cut it into cubes, and have the broccoli ready before heating the pan.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat, then sear the tofu for 4 to 5 minutes until the edges are golden.
Add the broccoli and carrot if using and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the vegetables are crisp-tender.
Stir in the soy sauce and ginger if using for 1 to 2 minutes until everything is glossy, then serve hot over rice if using.

name: Tomato Basil Pasta
instructions:
Fill a large pot about 2/3 full with water, add a good pinch of salt, and bring it to a boil.
Cook the pasta until tender with a little bite, stirring once after adding it, then reserve 1/2 cup pasta water and drain.
While the pasta cooks, heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet over medium-low heat and soften the garlic for 30 to 60 seconds until fragrant, not browned.
Stir in the tomato sauce and simmer over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes until it tastes savory and lightly concentrated.
Toss in the pasta with a splash of pasta water until the sauce looks glossy and coats the noodles.
Finish with basil, parmesan, or pepper if using and serve right away.

name: Creamy Tuna Noodle Casserole
instructions:
Heat the oven to 375F and cook the noodles for 6 to 8 minutes until just shy of tender so the casserole does not turn mushy.
Cook the onion if using in a skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Stir together the tuna, cream, noodles, peas, and onion, then spread the mixture evenly in a baking dish.
Top with cheddar if using and bake for 18 to 22 minutes until the edges bubble and the top is lightly golden.

name: Turkey Chili
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat and cook the turkey with the onion and garlic if using for 7 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains and browned bits form on the bottom.
Stir in the chili powder over medium heat and cook for 30 seconds until it smells toasty instead of raw.
Add the beans and crushed tomatoes, bring the pot to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer.
Cook for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring a few times, until the chili thickens into a hearty spoonable texture.
Top with cheddar or sour cream if using and serve hot enough to melt the cheddar at the edges.

name: Turkey Meatball Pasta
instructions:
Mix the ground turkey with a pinch of salt and pepper, then shape it into small meatballs about the size of a heaping tablespoon so they cook evenly.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the meatballs for 2 to 3 minutes per side until they hold together.
Add onion and garlic if using, then pour in the tomato sauce, lower the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the meatballs have no pink in the center or reach 165F.
While the sauce simmers, fill a large pot about 2/3 full with water, salt it lightly, and cook the pasta until just tender; reserve 1/2 cup pasta water and drain.
Spoon the meatballs and sauce over the pasta, loosen with a splash of pasta water if needed, and finish with parmesan if using.

name: Golden Vegetable Curry
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 to 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the curry powder and garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the potato, carrot, and coconut milk or tomatoes, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook over medium-low heat for 15 to 18 minutes until the vegetables are fork-tender and the sauce coats a spoon.
Stir in peas or spinach if using and cook 2 minutes more until heated through.
Season with salt, finish with lime if using, and serve hot over rice.

name: Veggie Black Bean Quesadillas
instructions:
Heat a skillet over medium heat with a small drizzle of oil and cook the bell pepper and onion for 4 to 5 minutes until tender and lightly browned.
Spread the beans on one half of each tortilla, add the vegetables and cheddar, then fold the tortillas closed.
Cook the quesadillas over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until the tortillas are crisp and golden brown and the cheese is fully melted.
Cut into wedges and serve hot with salsa.

name: Weeknight Beef Ragu
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta for 8 to 10 minutes until just tender; reserve a splash of pasta water before draining.
Heat a deep skillet over medium-high heat and cook the ground beef with the onion and garlic for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until the meat is browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the tomato sauce and simmer over medium-low heat for 4 to 5 minutes until slightly thickened and glossy.
Add the drained pasta and a splash of pasta water, then toss over medium-low heat for 1 minute until the noodles are coated; finish with parmesan if using.

name: Tomato Chicken Curry
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat and cook the onion with the garlic and curry powder for 3 to 4 minutes until the onion softens and the spices smell fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until the pieces lose their raw color and pick up light browning.
Stir in the tomato sauce and 1 cup water, then simmer over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the center and the sauce thickens.
Fold in the spinach for 1 minute until wilted if using, then serve hot with rice or flatbread.

name: Red Chicken Enchiladas
instructions:
Heat the oven to 375F and warm the tortillas for 20 to 30 seconds until they bend without cracking.
If you are starting with raw chicken, cook it in a skillet over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until it reaches 165F and is no longer pink, then shred or chop it.
Warm the enchilada sauce for 1 minute and spread a thin layer in a baking dish.
Fill each tortilla with chicken and a little cheese, then fold and roll it seam-side down in the dish.
Cover with the remaining sauce, black beans if using, and the rest of the cheese and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the sauce bubbles, then rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Creamy Chicken Enchilada Skillet
instructions:
Heat a deep skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken with the onion for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until the chicken is lightly browned and no longer pink on the outside.
Reduce the heat to medium, stir in the salsa and cream, and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce looks smooth and lightly thickened.
Tear the tortillas into strips and fold them into the skillet for 1 to 2 minutes so some pieces soften into the sauce while others stay a little structured.
Scatter the cheddar over the top, cover for 1 minute until melted, and serve when the chicken is cooked through and the skillet is bubbling lightly around the edges.

name: Beef Enchilada Casserole
instructions:
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the ground beef with the onion for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until the meat is browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the enchilada sauce and black beans if using, then simmer over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the filling thickens slightly.
Layer the tortillas, beef mixture, and cheddar in a baking dish, ending with sauce and cheese on top.
Bake at 400F for 18 to 22 minutes until the casserole is bubbling at the center and browned around the edges; rest for 5 minutes before scooping.

name: Street Corn Chicken Burrito Bowls
instructions:
Bring 2 cups water to a boil in a saucepan, stir in the rice, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 to 18 minutes until tender and fluffy.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5 to 7 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through with no pink in the center.
Add the corn to the same skillet and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until it picks up a little char at the edges, then stir in the salsa and a squeeze of lime.
Spoon the chicken and corn over the rice, top with cheddar if using, and serve while the bowls are hot and the rice stays fluffy.

name: Chicken Tinga Tostadas
instructions:
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat, add the chicken and onion if using, and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until the chicken is browned and cooked through.
Stir in the tomato sauce, reduce the heat to medium, and simmer for 5 to 6 minutes until the sauce is thick enough to cling to the chicken.
Warm or crisp the corn tortillas in a dry skillet for 1 to 2 minutes per side until sturdy for tostadas.
Pile the saucy chicken onto the tortillas, then top with lettuce and lime if using and serve while the shells are crisp.

name: Creamy White Chicken Chili
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 to 5 minutes until softened.
Add the chicken and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often, until the pieces lose most of their raw color and pick up light browning on the edges.
Stir in the green chiles, white beans, corn if using, and 2 cups water, then simmer gently for 12 to 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the beans begin to soften.
Mash a spoonful of the beans against the side of the pot, then stir in the cream for 1 to 2 minutes until the chili looks silky, lightly thickened, and clearly creamy instead of brothy.
Top with green onion if using and serve hot.

name: BBQ Chicken Stuffed Potatoes
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F, prick the potatoes, and bake them for 30 to 35 minutes until a knife slides through the centers easily.
Warm the chicken with BBQ sauce in a skillet over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the sauce bubbles and the chicken is hot throughout.
Split the potatoes, fluff the centers, and pile in the BBQ chicken so the sauce soaks into the potato.
Top with cheddar if using and bake for 3 to 5 minutes until melted, then finish with green onion and sour cream if using.

name: BBQ Sausage and Corn Skillet
instructions:
Heat a skillet over medium heat and cook the sausage for 6 to 8 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add onion and bell pepper if using and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the corn and BBQ sauce and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the corn is hot and the sauce turns glossy.
Serve straight from the skillet or with bread on the side.

name: Smothered Pork and Rice
instructions:
Heat a deep skillet over medium-high heat, then brown the pork for 5 to 6 minutes until the edges take on color.
Transfer the pork to a plate, add the onion, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until softened in the drippings.
Stir in the rice with enough liquid to cook it, return the pork, cover, and simmer over low heat for 16 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the pork is firm with no pink in the center.
Finish with garlic, pepper, or butter if using, and serve while the pan sauce is hot.

name: Garlic Lime Shrimp Tostadas
instructions:
Pat the shrimp dry, then season it with garlic, lime juice, and salt for 1 minute while the skillet heats.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes per side until pink, curled, and opaque.
Warm the tostadas for 1 minute in a dry skillet if they need crisping.
Toss cabbage with mayo or hot sauce if using, pile the shrimp onto the tostadas, and serve immediately so the shells stay crisp.

name: Smoky Red Beans and Rice
instructions:
Start the rice in a covered pot first and let it steam off the heat for 5 minutes while the beans finish.
Heat a skillet or saucepan over medium heat and cook the sausage with the onion, garlic, and pepper if using for 6 to 8 minutes until the sausage is browned and no pink remains.
Stir in the beans with a splash of broth or water and bring to a steady simmer.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring a few times, until some of the beans break down and the mixture turns thick and smoky.
Spoon the beans and sausage over the hot rice and let the bowls stand 1 minute before serving.

name: Calabacitas Bean Skillet
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium heat with a drizzle of oil and cook the onion and zucchini for 6 to 8 minutes until the zucchini is tender and lightly browned.
Stir in the corn, beans, and tomato sauce if using, then cook over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes until everything is hot throughout.
Sprinkle cheddar over the skillet if using and cook 1 minute more until melted.
Serve hot with tortillas or rice.

name: Spiced Lentil Rice Pilaf
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat with a drizzle of oil and cook the onion for 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic and warm spices for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the rice, lentils, and water, bring to a boil, then reduce to low, cover, and simmer for 22 to 25 minutes until the lentils are tender and the rice is fluffy.
Turn off the heat and let the pilaf sit covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Fold in spinach if using until wilted and serve warm with yogurt on the side.

name: Ginger Soy Salmon Cabbage Skillet
instructions:
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat, then sear the salmon for 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned and just opaque at the center.
Transfer the salmon to a plate, add the cabbage, ginger, and garlic if using, and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until wilted but still a little crisp.
Splash in the soy sauce and cook for 1 minute until it bubbles and coats the cabbage.
Return the salmon in large pieces and toss gently for 1 minute until warmed through, then serve with rice if using.

name: BBQ Pork Sweet Potato Hash
instructions:
Heat a covered skillet over medium heat with a little oil, then cook the sweet potato and onion if using for 8 to 10 minutes until the cubes start to soften.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium-high, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more until the sweet potato browns at the edges.
Add the pork and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until browned and firm with no pink in the center.
Stir in the BBQ sauce and corn if using for 2 minutes until sticky and savory, then finish with cheddar if using and serve hot.

name: Cajun Shrimp Rice Skillet
instructions:
Heat a deep skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and bell pepper for 4 to 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the rice, cajun seasoning if using, and enough water to cover the rice by about 1/2 inch, then bring the pan to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes until the rice is almost tender.
Fold in the shrimp and corn if using, cover again, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the shrimp are pink, opaque, and curled and the rice is fluffy.

name: Garlic Butter Shrimp and Broccoli
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the broccoli with 2 tablespoons water for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Push the broccoli to the edges, add the butter and garlic to the center, and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side until they are pink, opaque, and curled into loose C-shapes.
Finish with lemon and red pepper flakes if using, toss everything together, and serve right away.

name: Lemon Butter Baked Tilapia Packets
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and divide the broccoli between large sheets of parchment or foil.
Set the tilapia on top and season with lemon, garlic, pepper, and butter if using.
Seal the packets tightly, place them on a sheet pan, and bake for 14 to 16 minutes.
Open the packets carefully and serve when the tilapia is opaque and flakes easily with a fork and the broccoli is tender.

name: Cajun Salmon Sheet Pan
instructions:
Heat the oven to 425F and toss the green beans and sliced potatoes if using with the oil and half the cajun seasoning on a sheet pan.
Roast the vegetables for 10 minutes so they get a head start and begin to brown at the edges.
Rub the salmon with the remaining cajun seasoning, add it to the pan, and roast for 8 to 10 minutes more.
Finish with lemon and serve when the salmon is just opaque in the center and flakes easily and the vegetables are tender.

name: Spicy Tuna Tomato Pasta
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta for 8 to 10 minutes until just tender.
Warm the garlic and red pepper flakes in a skillet over medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato sauce and tuna and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce is hot and the tuna stays in chunky pieces.
Toss in the pasta with a splash of cooking water for 1 minute until coated, then finish with parmesan if using.

name: Cheesy Tuna Melt Quesadillas
instructions:
Fold the tuna with the mayo, hot sauce, and finely chopped onion if using until the filling holds together without looking wet.
Spread the tuna over half of each tortilla, top with cheddar so it melts quickly, and fold the tortillas closed.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and cook the quesadillas for 2 to 3 minutes per side until the tortillas are crisp and golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Let them stand for 1 minute, then slice and serve while hot.

name: Spicy Shrimp Sushi Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook until tender, then fold in the rice vinegar plus a pinch of sugar and salt so the base reads clearly as sushi-style rice instead of plain steamed rice.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat, add the shrimp with the soy sauce, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side until the shrimp are pink, opaque, and curled.
Whisk the mayo and sriracha until smooth, then build the bowls with the seasoned rice, warm shrimp, cucumber, and avocado if using.
Drizzle the spicy mayo over the bowls, toss on the green onion, and serve right away so the bowl keeps its hot-cold sushi-bowl contrast.

name: Teriyaki Salmon Edamame Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat until tender so it is hot when the bowls are assembled.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the salmon for 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned and nearly cooked through.
Add the teriyaki sauce and ginger if using, then simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, spooning the sauce over the fish, until the salmon flakes easily and the sauce turns glossy.
Warm the edamame for 1 to 2 minutes and slice the cucumber while the salmon rests.
Fold the glazed salmon and edamame over the rice with the cucumber on top, then spoon the extra teriyaki sauce from the pan over the bowls and finish with green onion if using.

name: Miso Ginger Cod Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender so it is ready when the cod finishes.
Whisk the miso and ginger with 2 tablespoons water, then simmer the mixture for 30 seconds so the bowl has a true miso-ginger sauce instead of plain pan juices.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil, add the cod, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side until the fish flakes easily in the center and the surface is lightly browned.
Add the cabbage and carrot if using during the last 2 minutes so they wilt slightly but still keep some bite, then pour in the miso-ginger mixture and let it bubble for 30 seconds until it coats the fish and vegetables.
Fold the cod and cabbage mixture over the rice, finish with green onion if using, and serve while the sauce is still glossy.

name: Honey Soy Shrimp Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the broccoli for 3 minutes with a splash of water until crisp-tender, then remove it to a plate.
Stir the soy sauce and honey together, add the shrimp, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side until pink, opaque, and curled.
Return the broccoli and carrot to the pan for 1 minute until coated in the sauce.
Build the bowls with rice, shrimp, and vegetables, then finish with green onion if using.

name: Crispy Tofu Sushi Bowls
instructions:
Cook the rice according to the package directions, then keep it covered for 5 minutes so it stays hot and steamy.
Pat the tofu dry, then cook it in a skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil for 6 to 8 minutes, turning occasionally, until the cubes are browned on multiple sides.
Add the soy sauce and sesame oil and cook 1 minute more until the tofu is glossy and hot throughout.
Build the bowls with rice, tofu, cucumber, and avocado if using, then drizzle with mayo and sriracha if using and toss lightly before serving.

name: Spicy Mayo Salmon Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook until tender, then let it steam off heat for a few minutes so the grains stay fluffy.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat, cook the salmon for 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned at the edges and the center reaches 145F or flakes easily, then rest it for 1 minute and break it into large pieces.
Whisk the mayo and sriracha until smooth, then toss the cucumber and green onion together so the cold toppings are ready.
Drizzle the spicy mayo over the rice, fold in the salmon and cold toppings, and serve right away so the bowl keeps its sushi-style contrast.

name: Korean-Inspired Beef Sesame Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat, add the beef, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the cabbage and carrot and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the cabbage starts to wilt but still has some crunch.
Toss in the sesame oil and sriracha if using for 1 minute.
Spoon the beef and vegetables over the rice and finish with green onion if using.

name: Korean-Inspired Chicken Cabbage Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat until tender.
Stir the soy sauce and gochujang together with a spoonful of water and the sesame oil if using so the sauce is ready when the chicken comes off the heat.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat, add the chicken, and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until browned in spots and cooked through to 165F.
Add the cabbage and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until it softens but still keeps some crunch.
Pour in the sauce and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, tossing often, until the chicken and cabbage look glossy and evenly coated.
Divide the rice into bowls, top with the chicken and cabbage mixture, then finish with cucumber and green onion if using. The bowl should eat like a savory-spicy rice bowl with warm glazed chicken, tender-crisp cabbage, and a cool fresh finish.

name: Teriyaki Chicken Broccoli Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned at the edges and no longer pink in the center.
Add the broccoli and carrot if using with teriyaki sauce and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the vegetables are crisp-tender and coated.
Layer the rice with the chicken, broccoli, carrot, and pan sauce, then finish with green onion if using and serve while hot.

name: Miso Salmon Bok Choy Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Stir the miso with 2 tablespoons water and simmer for 1 minute to make a quick sauce.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat, add the salmon, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side until the center flakes easily.
Add the bok choy and carrot during the last 2 minutes, then pour in the miso sauce and cook until the vegetables are crisp-tender and glazed.
Spoon the salmon and vegetables over the rice and finish with green onion if using.

name: Ginger Sesame Tuna Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Stir the ginger, sesame oil, and mayo into the tuna for 1 minute until the mixture is evenly coated.
Warm the tuna and edamame in a skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until hot throughout.
Toss the hot rice with the tuna and edamame for 1 minute, then top with cucumber and green onion and serve right away.

name: Garlic Sesame Chicken Noodle Bowls
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles until just tender, about 6 to 8 minutes, reserving 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with the sesame oil, add the chicken and garlic, and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until the chicken is browned in spots and cooked through with no pink remaining. Add the carrot and green onion if using and cook for 2 minutes until the vegetables soften slightly but still keep some bite. Add the noodles and soy sauce, then splash in enough reserved noodle water to make a light savory coating. Toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until the noodles are glossy, smell nutty from the sesame oil, and stay evenly coated instead of dry.

name: Soy Ginger Shrimp Lo Mein
instructions:
Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the noodles until just tender.
Reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil.
Add the shrimp and cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side until they are pink, opaque, and curled into loose C-shapes.
Add the ginger with the soy sauce, cabbage, and carrot if using, then stir-fry for 2 minutes so the vegetables soften slightly but still keep some crunch.
Toss in the noodles with a splash of the reserved cooking water and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the noodles are glossy and coated.
Finish with green onion if using and serve right away.

name: Miso Butter Salmon Noodles
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles until just tender, about 6 to 8 minutes, reserving 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat, melt the butter if using, and whisk in the miso with 2 tablespoons of the noodle water for 30 seconds until smooth.
Add the salmon and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side, spooning the miso butter over the fish, until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Add the spinach and green onion if using and cook for 1 minute until the spinach wilts.
Toss in the noodles with a splash of reserved noodle water over medium-low heat for 1 minute until coated and glossy.

name: Chili Garlic Beef Noodles
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles until just tender, about 6 to 8 minutes, reserving 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the beef with the garlic for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking up or stirring the meat until it is browned and hot through.
Add the chili sauce and soy sauce with the cabbage and carrot if using, then cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the vegetables are crisp-tender and the sauce bubbles around the beef.
Add the drained noodles with a splash of the reserved noodle water and toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce clings to the noodles.
Top with green onion if using and serve while hot.

name: Sesame Peanut Chicken Noodles
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles until just tender, about 6 to 8 minutes, reserving 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned at the edges and cooked through with no pink remaining.
Whisk the peanut butter and soy sauce with 1/4 cup of the reserved noodle water, pour that sauce into the skillet, and cook over medium heat for 1 minute until smooth.
Add the noodles with the cucumber and green onion if using, then toss for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce evenly coats the noodles and everything is hot.
Serve right away while the noodles are glossy.

name: Sesame Edamame Udon Bowls
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the udon or other noodles until just tender, about 6 to 8 minutes, reserving 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with the sesame oil and cook the tofu for 4 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until it is browned on the edges.
Add the edamame and soy sauce, then cook for 2 minutes over medium heat until the edamame is hot throughout and the sauce smells toasty.
Add the noodles with the cucumber and green onion if using, splash in a little reserved noodle water, and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until everything is evenly coated and steaming.
Serve while hot.

name: Spicy Shrimp Peanut Noodles
instructions:
Boil the noodles until just tender, reserving 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Whisk the peanut butter with a few spoonfuls of the hot noodle water and the pantry sauce ingredients until smooth.
Sear the shrimp in a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 minutes per side until pink, opaque, and curled.
Add the drained noodles, peanut sauce, and carrot if using, then toss for 1 to 2 minutes until glossy and evenly coated.
Fold in the cucumber and green onion off the heat and serve while the noodles are still hot.

name: Ginger Garlic Pork Noodles
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles until just tender, about 6 to 8 minutes, reserving 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the pork with the ginger and garlic for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until the pork is browned and cooked through.
Add the cabbage and carrot if using and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the vegetables soften slightly but still keep some texture.
Add the soy sauce, noodles, and a splash of the reserved noodle water, then toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until the noodles are coated and steaming.
Top with green onion if using and serve hot.

name: Soy Mushroom Cabbage Noodles
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles until just tender, about 6 to 8 minutes, reserving 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the tofu for 4 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until it is browned on several sides.
Add the mushrooms and cabbage if using and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the mushrooms release their moisture and the cabbage is crisp-tender.
Add the soy sauce and sesame oil if using with the noodles and a splash of reserved noodle water, then toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until everything is glossy and hot.
Finish with green onion if using and serve right away.

name: Coconut Curry Chicken Noodles
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles until just tender, about 6 to 8 minutes; reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes until it is browned in spots and cooked through with no pink remaining. Stir in the curry paste and coconut milk, reduce to medium heat, and simmer for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly. Add the carrot and green onion if using and cook for 2 minutes, then toss in the noodles and a squeeze of lime if using; cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the noodles are coated and the sauce is bubbling gently.

name: Teriyaki Salmon Noodle Bowls
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil over high heat and cook the noodles for 6 to 8 minutes until just tender; reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining. Heat a skillet over medium heat, add the salmon with the teriyaki sauce and ginger, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily. Add the broccoli and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp-tender. Toss in the noodles with a splash of the reserved cooking water and cook over medium-low heat for 1 to 2 minutes until glossy and coated.

name: Chili Sesame Tofu Noodles
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles until just tender, about 6 to 8 minutes, reserving 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with the sesame oil and cook the tofu for 4 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until it is browned on several sides.
Add the chili sauce, soy sauce, cabbage, and carrot if using, then cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the vegetables are crisp-tender and the sauce bubbles lightly.
Add the noodles with a splash of reserved noodle water and toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until everything is glossy and hot.
Finish with green onion if using and serve right away.

name: Black Pepper Beef Broccoli Stir-Fry
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil.
Add the thinly sliced steak and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until browned at the edges, then transfer it to a plate so it stays tender.
Add the broccoli and carrot if using with 2 tablespoons of water, cover, and steam for 2 minutes until the broccoli turns bright green.
Uncover and stir-fry the vegetables over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 minutes until they are crisp-tender.
Stir the soy sauce, garlic, and black pepper together, return the steak to the skillet, and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce lightly coats the beef and broccoli.
