Serve right away over rice if using while the beef stays glossy and the broccoli still has some bite.

name: Garlic Sesame Shrimp Stir-Fry
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil. Add the shrimp and garlic and cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side until the shrimp turn pink and opaque and curl into loose C-shapes. Add the broccoli and carrot if using and cook over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the vegetables are crisp-tender. Stir in the soy sauce and green onion for 1 minute until the shrimp and broccoli are glossy and coated. Serve over hot rice if using.

name: Ginger Snap Pea Chicken Stir-Fry
instructions: If using rice, start it first. Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil, then cook the chicken with ginger if using for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned and cooked through with no pink remaining. Add the carrot first if using and cook for 1 minute, then add the snap peas and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender. Pour in the soy sauce and the remaining pantry sauce ingredients, toss for 1 minute until the chicken and vegetables are glossy, then finish with green onion and serve over rice if using.

name: Teriyaki Tofu Broccoli Stir-Fry
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a thin film of oil. Add the tofu and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until the edges are browned and the center is hot. Add the broccoli and carrot if using and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes until the broccoli is crisp-tender. Stir in the teriyaki sauce and green onion, toss for 1 to 2 minutes until the tofu and broccoli are coated, and serve over rice if using.

name: Chili Garlic Salmon Stir-Fry
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil.
Cook the salmon for 2 to 3 minutes per side until browned on the outside and the center flakes easily, then move it to a plate.
Add the cabbage and carrot if using with a pinch of salt and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the cabbage softens but still has some bite.
Stir in the soy sauce, the remaining pantry sauce ingredients, and sriracha if using, then return the salmon to the pan and toss gently for 1 minute until coated and heated through.
Top with green onion and serve over rice if using.

name: Sesame Green Bean Pork Stir-Fry
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil. Add the pork and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until the pork is browned and the center is no longer pink. Add the green beans and carrot if using and cook over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the beans are bright green and just tender. Stir in the soy sauce with a drizzle of sesame oil, toss for 1 to 2 minutes until the pork and green beans are coated, and serve over rice if using.

name: Honey Soy Chicken Pepper Stir-Fry
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil. Add the chicken and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until browned in spots and cooked through with no pink remaining. Add the bell pepper and onion if using and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes until the vegetables start to soften but still keep some bite. Stir in the soy sauce with honey and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the chicken and peppers are glossy and coated. Finish with green onion and serve over rice if using.

name: Miso Shrimp Vegetable Stir-Fry
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil. Add the shrimp and cook with the miso for 1 to 2 minutes per side until the shrimp are pink, opaque, and curled into loose C-shapes. Add the broccoli and carrot if using and cook over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the vegetables are crisp-tender. Stir in the green onion and any extra sauce from the pan, toss for 1 minute until the shrimp and vegetables are coated, and serve over rice if using.

name: Garlic Bok Choy Beef Stir-Fry
instructions:
Slice the steak thinly and pat it dry so it browns quickly in the wok.
Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat, then sear the steak with garlic if using for 2 to 3 minutes until browned at the edges and still juicy.
Add the bok choy, mushrooms, or green onion if using and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the stems are crisp-tender and the leaves wilt.
Pour in the soy sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until the stir-fry turns shiny and clings lightly to the steak and vegetables, then serve hot with rice if using.

name: Sesame Edamame Tofu Stir-Fry
instructions:
Pat the tofu dry, cut it into cubes, and set the rice to cook first if using.
Cook the tofu in a hot skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil and sesame oil if using for 6 to 8 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned on several sides.
Add the edamame and carrot if using, then stir-fry for 2 minutes until the edamame is hot and the carrot starts to soften.
Pour in the soy sauce and the remaining pantry sauce ingredients, then toss for 1 minute until the tofu is coated and glossy.
Finish with green onion and serve over rice if using.

name: Ginger Carrot Chicken Stir-Fry
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil. Add the chicken and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring every minute, until the pieces are browned and no longer pink in the center; add the ginger and garlic if using during the last minute. Add the carrots and cabbage if using and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the carrots are tender-crisp and the cabbage is soft. Pour in the soy sauce and stir for 30 seconds until the sauce covers the chicken and vegetables. Spoon over rice and top with green onion if using.

name: Sweet Soy Salmon Broccoli Stir-Fry
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil.
Cook the salmon for 2 to 3 minutes per side until browned and just cooked through, then move it to a plate.
Add the broccoli and carrot if using with a splash of water, cover for 1 minute, and cook 1 to 2 minutes more until the broccoli is crisp-tender.
Stir in the soy sauce and the remaining pantry sauce ingredients, then return the salmon to the pan and toss gently for 1 minute until glossy and heated through.
Finish with green onion and serve over rice if using.

name: Salmon Edamame Fried Rice
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with sesame oil if using. Add the salmon and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until the center is opaque and the fish flakes with a fork; add the ginger if using during the last minute. Break the salmon into bite-size pieces and move it to one side of the pan. Scramble the egg on the open side until just set, then add the rice, edamame, and carrot if using and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the rice is hot and a few grains are browned. Stir in the green onion if using and serve hot.

name: Pineapple Shrimp Fried Rice
instructions:
Use cold rice if you have it so the grains stay separate in the pan.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes per side with a light splash of soy sauce until the shrimp turn pink and curl, then move them to a plate.
Add the pineapple and carrot if using to the same skillet and cook for 2 minutes until the pineapple is hot and lightly caramelized at the edges.
Push the pineapple mixture to one side, scramble the egg until just set, then add the rice and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the grains pick up color.
Return the shrimp to the pan, season with the remaining soy sauce, fold in the green onion if using, and serve while the salty rice and sweet pineapple still balance each other.

name: Beef Broccoli Fried Rice
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with sesame oil if using. Add the beef and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it up as needed, until browned and cooked through; add the ginger if using during the last minute. Push the beef to one side, scramble the egg on the open side until just set, then add the rice, broccoli, and carrot if using. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the broccoli is crisp-tender and the rice is hot with a few browned edges. Stir in the green onion if using and serve hot.

name: Tofu Carrot Fried Rice
instructions:
Use cold rice if you have it and break up any clumps so the grains stay separate in the pan.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat, then cook the tofu for 4 to 5 minutes until browned at the edges.
Push the tofu to the side, scramble the egg for 1 to 2 minutes until just set, then add the carrot and peas if using.
Add the rice and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the grains are hot and lightly toasted, then finish with green onion and sesame oil if using.

name: Pork Cabbage Fried Rice
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the pork with ginger for 4 to 5 minutes until browned and no pink remains.
Add the cabbage and any carrot, then cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Push the pork mixture to one side, add the egg, and scramble for 30 to 60 seconds until just set.
Add the cold rice and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until hot and lightly browned in spots.
Fold in the green onion and sesame oil, if using, and serve.

name: Miso Mushroom Fried Rice
instructions:
Use cold rice if you have it so the grains stay separate in the pan.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with the sesame oil if using and cook the mushrooms for 3 to 4 minutes until browned and their moisture cooks off.
Add the tofu and cook for 3 minutes more until the cubes are crisp on the edges, then push the mushrooms and tofu to one side and scramble the egg until just set.
Stir the miso with the soy sauce and 1 to 2 tablespoons water, add the rice and carrot if using, and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the grains are hot and lightly toasted.
Pour in the miso-soy mixture, fold everything together until the rice is evenly coated, then finish with green onion if using.

name: Chili Garlic Shrimp Fried Rice
instructions:
Use cold rice if you have it so the grains stay separate in the pan instead of steaming together.
Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat with a little oil, add the shrimp, garlic, and chili sauce, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side until the shrimp turn pink, curl, and smell spicy instead of raw. Transfer the shrimp to a plate.
Add the carrot if using and cook for 1 minute, then push it to one side and scramble the egg until just set.
Add the rice and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the grains are hot, separate, and picking up color in spots. Return the shrimp, add the soy sauce and sesame oil if using, and toss for 1 minute until the rice is evenly seasoned.
Toss with green onion if using and serve hot so the final fried rice stays clearly chili-garlic forward and distinct from sweeter shrimp fried rice variations.

name: Miso Glazed Salmon with Rice
instructions:
Roast the salmon and broccoli at 425F for 10 to 12 minutes, spreading the miso over the salmon if using and drizzling the broccoli with sesame oil if using, until the salmon reaches 145F or flakes easily and the broccoli has browned edges.
Toss the broccoli in the pan juices for 30 seconds, then set the salmon and broccoli over the rice.
Rest the pan for 1 minute, then scatter green onion if using over the bowls and serve.

name: Soy Ginger Baked Cod with Rice
instructions:
Heat the oven to 425F and line a sheet pan so the cod and vegetables roast in one intentional oven step.
Toss the cabbage and carrot if using with a little oil, spread them on the pan, and roast for 5 minutes so they start to soften before the fish goes in.
Stir the soy sauce and ginger together, brush half over the cod, then add the cod to the pan and roast for 8 to 10 minutes more until the fish reaches 145F or flakes easily in the center.
Brush the cod with the remaining soy-ginger glaze for the last 2 minutes of cooking, toss the cabbage and carrot in the hot pan juices, and serve everything over the rice with green onion or sesame oil if using.

name: Sesame Ginger Salmon Sheet Pan
instructions:
Roast the salmon, green beans, and carrot if using at 425F for 10 to 12 minutes, drizzling the pan with soy sauce if using, until the salmon reaches 145F or flakes easily and the vegetables are tender-crisp with browned spots.
Toss the green beans and carrot in the pan juices for 30 seconds, then set the salmon and vegetables over the rice.
Rest the pan for 1 minute, then scatter green onion if using over the bowls and serve.

name: Miso Butter Shrimp Foil Packets
instructions:
Fold the shrimp, broccoli, carrot if using, and miso if using into a sealed foil packet set on a sheet pan, then roast at 425F for 10 to 12 minutes until the shrimp are pink, opaque, and curled and the broccoli is tender.
Rest the packet for 1 minute, then open it carefully to release the steam.
Toss the shrimp and vegetables in the packet juices for 30 seconds and serve over rice with green onion if using.

name: Sticky Soy Chicken Thigh Tray
instructions:
Roast the chicken thighs over the cabbage and carrot if using at 425F for 20 to 22 minutes, scattering the garlic over the vegetables if using, until the chicken reaches 165F and the cabbage has browned edges.
Scatter the green onion over the pan for the last 2 minutes if using, then rest the pan for 1 minute.
Toss the cabbage in the pan juices for 30 seconds and spoon the chicken and vegetables over rice.

name: Japanese-Inspired Chicken Curry Rice
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat and cook the potato with the onion and carrot, if using, for 4 to 5 minutes until the onion is softened.
Stir in the curry powder, add the chicken, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the pieces are opaque on the outside.
Add enough water to mostly cover the chicken and vegetables, bring to a gentle boil, then lower to medium-low heat.
Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the potato is fork-tender and the chicken reaches 165F.
Fold the mashed potato back into the broth to thicken the curry, then serve over hot rice.

name: Japanese-Inspired Beef Curry Bowls
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion if using for 3 to 4 minutes until softened, then stir in the curry powder if using for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the beef, potato, carrot if using, and enough water to come just below the beef and vegetables, then bring the pot to a boil.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover partially, and simmer for 18 to 20 minutes until the beef is cooked through, the potatoes are fork-tender, and the broth is lightly thickened. Spoon the curry over hot rice and serve.

name: Thai-Inspired Tofu Green Bean Curry
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a pot over medium heat with a splash of oil, then cook the bell pepper and green beans if using for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Stir in the tofu and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the edges are golden and the center is hot.
Add the coconut milk and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon, then finish with lime if using and serve over the rice.

name: Chipotle Shrimp Tacos
instructions:
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 to 30 seconds per side so they stay flexible.
Cook the shrimp over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 minutes per side until they are pink, opaque, and curled into loose C-shapes.
Squeeze in the lime and toss in the cabbage if using for 30 seconds until lightly wilted.
Fill the tortillas with the shrimp and top with mayo and cilantro if using.

name: Garlic Lime Fish Tacos
instructions:
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 to 30 seconds per side so they stay flexible.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat, then cook the white fish with garlic if using for 3 to 4 minutes on the first side until browned at the edges.
Flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more, squeezing in the lime, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Fill the tortillas with the fish, cabbage and mayo if using, then finish with cilantro and serve while the tortillas are soft.

name: Adobo Chicken Tacos
instructions:
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 to 30 seconds per side so they stay flexible.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until browned at the edges.
Stir in the tomato sauce and onion if using, then simmer over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes until the sauce clings to the chicken and the center is no longer pink.
Pile the saucy chicken into the tortillas, finish with cilantro and lime if using, and serve right away while the filling is hot.

name: Chile Lime Beef Tacos
instructions:
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 to 30 seconds per side until soft and pliable.
Cook the ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the onion if using with chili powder, salt, and the juice from half the lime, then cook 2 minutes until the onion softens and the beef smells bright and lightly spiced.
Fill the tortillas with the beef, top with salsa and cilantro if using, and serve right away while the filling is hot and the tortillas stay tender.

name: Crispy Potato Poblano Tacos
instructions:
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 to 30 seconds per side so they stay flexible.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat with a thin layer of oil, then cook the potato and onion for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potato is browned and tender.
Add the poblano if using and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Fill the tortillas with the crispy potato mixture, add cheddar and cilantro if using, and serve while the filling is hot.

name: Salsa Verde Shrimp Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes until tender.
Cook the shrimp with the salsa verde in a skillet over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 minutes per side until the shrimp are pink, opaque, and curled.
Add the cabbage if using and cook for 1 minute until just wilted.
Serve the shrimp over the rice and finish with lime and cilantro if using.

name: Chipotle Salmon Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat, then cook the salmon for 3 to 4 minutes on the first side until browned at the edges.
Flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more with lime until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Warm the corn or cabbage if using for 1 to 2 minutes, then spoon the salmon over the rice and finish with cilantro if using.

name: Calabacitas Chicken Skillet
instructions:
Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat, add the chicken and onion if using, and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until the chicken is browned and cooked through.
Add the zucchini and corn, then cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the zucchini is tender but not collapsing and the corn is hot.
Reduce the heat to medium, fold in cheddar if using, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until melted.
Finish with cilantro if using and serve hot while the vegetables still have some texture.

name: Salsa Roja Beef Rice Skillet
instructions: Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat and cook the beef with the onion for 4 to 5 minutes, turning the pieces, until browned at the edges and hot in the center. Stir in the rice, salsa, corn, plus enough water to cook the rice and bring the pan to a boil. Cover and cook over low heat for 15 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed. Uncover and cook for 1 to 2 minutes if the skillet still looks loose. Finish with cilantro and serve while still steaming.

name: Poblano Bean Enchiladas
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F for at least 10 minutes and spread a spoonful of salsa verde across the bottom of a baking dish.
Cook the poblano in a skillet over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes until tender, then stir in the black beans and a few spoonfuls of salsa verde and cook 2 minutes more until hot throughout.
Fill the tortillas with the bean mixture and a little cheddar if using, roll closed, and arrange them seam-side down in the dish before spooning the remaining salsa verde over the top.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the sauce is bubbling and the cheese is melted with browned spots, then rest 5 minutes and finish with cilantro if using.

name: Lime Cabbage Shrimp Taco Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, then cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes per side until pink, opaque, and curled. Toss in the cabbage and corn if using for 1 to 2 minutes until the cabbage softens slightly but still has some crunch.
Let the skillet sit off the heat for 1 minute, then spoon the shrimp mixture over the rice and drizzle with the mayo and cilantro if using.

name: Chile Lime Tilapia Plates
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, then cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a skillet over medium and cook the tilapia with the lime for 3 to 4 minutes per side until the fish flakes easily and is opaque all the way through. Add the corn and cabbage if using for 1 to 2 minutes until warmed through and the cabbage starts to soften.
Rest the tilapia for 1 minute, then serve it over the rice with cilantro if using.

name: Roasted Corn Black Bean Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, then cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a skillet over medium and cook the corn for 2 minutes until hot and lightly charred in spots. Stir in the black beans with 2 tablespoons of water and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the beans are hot and the liquid has mostly cooked away.
Toss in the cabbage if using for 1 minute until just wilted, then spoon the corn and beans over the rice and top with cheddar and cilantro if using.

name: Tomato Braised Pork Tacos
instructions:
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 to 30 seconds per side, or wrap them in foil and keep them warm.
Cook the pork in a skillet over medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and no pink remains. Stir in the tomato sauce and onion if using, then simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Toss the cilantro and lime if using over the filled tacos and serve right away while the tortillas are still soft.

name: Chicken Tortilla Rice Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat with a splash of oil, then simmer the tomato sauce for 2 to 3 minutes until it darkens slightly and bubbles steadily.
Add the chicken, rice, and chicken broth if using, then bring the pot to a steady simmer over medium-high heat.
Cook over medium-low heat for 16 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken is no longer pink in the center.
Warm the corn tortillas for 1 to 2 minutes if using, then ladle the soup hot with lime and cilantro if using.

name: Shrimp Calabacitas Skillet
instructions:
Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat, add the onion if using, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the zucchini and corn and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the zucchini is tender and the corn is hot.
Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring often, until the shrimp are pink, curled, and opaque.
Finish with cilantro if using and serve over rice if using while the skillet is hot.

name: Beef Picadillo Rice Bowls
instructions: Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender. Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the potato with a splash of oil for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it starts to soften and brown at the edges. Add the ground beef and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it up, until the meat is browned and no pink remains, then stir in the carrot and peas if using with cumin and a splash of water. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the potato is tender and the beef mixture turns thick and savory, then spoon it over the rice and finish with cilantro if using.

name: Pinto Bean Sweet Potato Tacos
instructions:
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 to 30 seconds per side so they stay flexible.
Cook the sweet potato in a covered skillet over medium heat with a splash of oil and water for 8 to 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the pinto beans and cook uncovered for 3 to 4 minutes, mashing some beans against the pan until the filling is hot and lightly thickened.
Fill the tortillas with the sweet potato and bean mixture, then finish with lime, cilantro, and cheddar if using.

name: Mushroom Poblano Enchiladas
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and lightly oil a baking dish for 1 minute while you warm the tortillas.
Cook the mushrooms and poblano if using in a skillet over medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes until browned and the moisture cooks off.
Fill the tortillas with the mushroom mixture, roll them into the dish, and spoon salsa verde over the top so the tortillas stay coated.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes until the sauce bubbles at the edges and the tortillas are tender, then rest for 5 minutes and finish with cheddar or cilantro if using.

name: Queso Chicken Skillet Rice
instructions:
Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Stir in the rice with salsa and corn if using, then cook over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the rice is hot and the mixture is no longer watery.
Scatter the cheddar over the skillet, cover, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the cheese melts into a queso-style topping.
Finish with green onion if using and serve hot from the skillet.

name: Beef Fajita Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes until tender.
Cook the sliced steak in a skillet over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the bell pepper and onion if using and cook for 3 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp, then squeeze in the lime if using.
Serve the steak and peppers over the rice and top with cheddar if using.

name: Salsa Verde Turkey Burrito Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the ground turkey for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the black beans, salsa verde if using, and corn if using, then simmer over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until saucy and hot throughout.
Spoon the turkey mixture over the rice, finish with lime and cheddar if using, and serve while glossy.

name: Cheesy Beef Enchilada Rice Skillet
instructions: Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat and cook the beef for 4 to 5 minutes, turning the pieces, until browned at the edges and hot in the center. Stir in the rice, tomato sauce, black beans, plus enough water to cook the rice and bring the skillet to a boil. Cover and cook over low heat for 16 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the sauce looks thick instead of watery. Sprinkle cheddar over the top and cover for 1 minute until melted. Finish with green onion and serve hot from the skillet.

name: Fajita Shrimp Burrito Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat, then cook the bell pepper and onion if using for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp-tender and browned in spots.
Add the shrimp and cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side until pink, opaque, and curled into loose C-shapes, then squeeze in the lime if using.
Spoon the shrimp and peppers over the rice, add cheddar if using, and serve within 1 to 2 minutes while the pan juices are still glossy.

name: Street Corn Shrimp Bowls
instructions: Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender. Cook the corn in a skillet over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until hot with a few charred spots. Add the shrimp and cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side until pink, opaque, and curled, then squeeze in the lime if using. Spoon the shrimp and corn over the rice and finish with mayo and cilantro if using for a street-corn style topping.

name: Beef Taco Soup
instructions: Heat a soup pot over medium-high heat and cook the ground beef for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink remaining. Stir in the tomato sauce, black beans, plus the corn if using with 2 cups of water and bring the soup to a boil. Reduce the heat to a steady simmer and cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the broth tastes seasoned and the beans are hot all the way through. Ladle into bowls and finish with cheddar and green onion if using while the soup is still steaming hot.

name: White Bean Chicken Enchilada Soup
instructions:
Bring a soup pot to medium heat and add the chicken with a small splash of oil. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pieces lose their raw color and pick up a little browning on the edges.
Stir in the salsa verde and let it cook for 1 minute so it turns fragrant and coats the chicken, then add the chicken broth, white beans, and corn if using. Bring the pot to a gentle boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the beans have flavored the broth.
Mash a spoonful of the white beans against the side of the pot for 30 seconds so the broth turns slightly creamy and thickened.
Ladle into bowls and top with cheddar, green onion, plus crushed corn tortillas if using while the soup is still hot enough to melt the cheese.

name: Fajita Chicken Sheet Pan
instructions: Roast the chicken, bell pepper, and onion at 425F for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the vegetables are tender and the chicken is browned in spots and reaches 165F. Toss the hot chicken and vegetables with lime juice if using. Warm the flour tortillas for 1 to 2 minutes and spoon in the chicken and vegetables, melting cheddar on top if using.

name: Taco Spiced Salmon Bowls
instructions: Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender. Rub the salmon with taco seasoning, then cook it in a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Add the corn and black beans if using to the skillet for 1 to 2 minutes until warmed through and coated with the salmon spices. Spoon everything over the rice and serve with lime and cilantro if using while the salmon is still hot.

name: Queso Black Bean Burrito Bowls
instructions: Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender. Warm the black beans in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water for 3 to 4 minutes until hot and lightly thickened. Stir in the cheddar and cook for 1 minute over low heat until it melts into the beans and turns glossy. Spoon the queso beans over the rice and finish with corn, lime, and green onion if using.

name: Chipotle Chicken Corn Chowder
instructions: Heat a soup pot over medium heat and cook the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until it loses its raw color and picks up a little browning. Add the potato and corn with enough broth or water to cover everything by about 1 inch, bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the potato is tender and the chicken is cooked through. Stir in the milk and cook for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat until the chowder is hot and lightly creamy without boiling hard. Taste and adjust with salt and pepper, then top with cheddar and green onion if using and serve hot.

name: Creamy Poblano Chicken Bowls
instructions: Bring the rice to a boil first, cover, and cook over low heat until tender. Heat a skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil, then cook the chicken and sliced poblano for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is browned and no longer pink in the center and the poblano is tender. Stir in the corn if using and cook for 2 minutes until hot, then spoon the mixture over the rice. Finish with lime and cheddar if using so the cheese softens from the heat.

name: Smoky Pork Taco Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil, then cook the pork for 5 to 6 minutes until browned at the edges.
Stir in the black beans and corn if using, lower the heat to medium, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the beans are hot and the pork is firm with no pink in the center.
Spoon the smoky pork and beans over the rice, finish with lime and cheddar if using, and serve within 1 to 2 minutes while hot.

name: Green Chile Beef Rice Bowls
instructions: Cook the rice first so it is ready when the beef finishes. Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the ground beef for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink remaining. Stir in the green chiles and a pinch of cumin, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for 2 minutes until the chiles coat the beef and smell mellow instead of raw. Fold in the corn if using and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until hot, then spoon the beef over the rice and finish with cheddar and lime if using.

name: Bean and Cheese Enchilada Bake
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F for at least 10 minutes and lightly coat a baking dish with enchilada sauce if using.
Warm the black beans in a skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes with the corn if using until the filling is hot and lightly thickened.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat until flexible, then layer them in the dish with the beans and cheddar.
Spoon enchilada sauce over the top if using and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the cheese melts and the center is hot, then rest for 5 minutes and finish with green onion if using.

name: Fajita Veggie Taco Bowls
instructions: Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender. Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the bell pepper and onion if using for 4 to 5 minutes until tender-crisp with a few browned spots. Stir in the black beans with a pinch of chili powder and cumin and cook for 2 minutes until the beans are hot and the peppers smell lightly charred. Squeeze in the lime, spoon the fajita vegetables and beans over the rice, and serve with cheddar if using while the peppers are still hot.

name: Street Corn Turkey Burrito Bowls
instructions: Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender. Cook the ground turkey in a skillet over medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink remaining. Stir in the corn and cook for 2 minutes until hot with a few browned spots, then squeeze in the lime if using. Spoon the turkey and corn over the rice and finish with mayo, cilantro, and cheddar if using for a street-corn style bowl.

name: Cajun Catfish Rice Bowls
instructions:
Start the rice first and keep it covered so it stays hot for serving.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat, then cook the catfish for 3 to 4 minutes on the first side until browned at the edges.
Flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Warm the corn in the skillet for 1 to 2 minutes, then spoon the catfish and corn over the rice with green onion, lime, or hot sauce if using.

name: Smothered Chicken Onion Gravy
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until golden at the edges.
Add the onion and garlic if using, then cook for 3 to 4 minutes until softened and the chicken is no longer pink in the center.
Simmer the pan juices over medium heat for 2 minutes until lightly thickened, then spoon the chicken and onion gravy over the rice with green beans if using.

name: Creole Chicken Rice Skillet
instructions: Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat with a tablespoon of oil. Add the chicken and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it is browned and cooked through with no pink in the thickest pieces. Stir in the bell pepper, onion, and celery if using and cook for 3 minutes until they start to soften. Add the rice and stir for 1 minute so the grains get coated in the pan juices, then pour in 3 cups of water and bring the skillet to a boil. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Rest for 5 minutes, then scatter green onion over the top before serving.

name: Creole Shrimp Tomato Rice
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a wide skillet over medium heat, then cook the bell pepper and celery if using for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the tomato sauce and simmer for 2 minutes until it bubbles and tastes seasoned.
Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink, opaque, and curled, then spoon the Creole tomato shrimp over the rice with green onion if using.

name: Blackened Tilapia with Dirty Rice
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat, then cook the bell pepper, onion, and celery if using for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Season the tilapia, add it to the skillet, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes on the first side until browned.
Flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, then serve over the rice with green onion if using.

name: Cajun Sausage Green Bean Skillet
instructions:
Cut the potato into small pieces, then microwave or simmer it for 4 to 5 minutes until barely tender so it browns quickly in the skillet.
Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat and cook the sausage with cajun seasoning for 4 to 5 minutes until browned at the edges.
Add the potato, green beans, garlic, and pepper if using, then cook for 6 to 8 minutes until the beans are crisp-tender and the potatoes are golden.
Finish with green onion if using and serve hot while the sausage edges are still crisp.

name: Cajun Chicken Pasta
instructions:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until just tender. Reserve 1/2 cup of the pasta water before draining.
Toss the chicken with the cajun seasoning so it is coated on all sides. Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil and cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned in spots and cooked through to 165F. If using bell pepper, add it during the last 2 to 3 minutes so it softens but still keeps some bite.
Lower the heat to medium and pour in the cream, scraping up any seasoned bits from the skillet. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce looks lightly thickened and the cajun seasoning has flavored the cream instead of tasting raw.
Add the pasta and parmesan if using, then toss with splashes of the reserved pasta water until the noodles are evenly coated in a glossy, lightly spicy sauce. Finish with green onion if using and serve hot. The final pasta should read clearly as cajun chicken pasta: savory, peppery, creamy, and bold enough to justify the name.

name: Shrimp and Sausage Foil Packets
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and tear four large pieces of foil, giving the oven about 5 minutes to fully heat.
Toss the shrimp, sausage, corn, and potato if using with salt, then divide between the foil pieces, dot with butter if using, and seal the packets tightly.
Bake the packets for 14 to 16 minutes until the shrimp are pink, curled, and opaque and the sausage is hot.
Open the packets carefully for 1 minute to release steam, finish with green onion if using, and serve while the corn is juicy and hot.

name: Blackened Fish Sheet Pan
instructions:
Heat the oven to 425F and cut the potato into small pieces so it roasts before the fish overcooks.
Toss the potato and green beans with paprika, pepper, salt, and a little oil, then spread them on a sheet pan and roast for 12 minutes.
Season the white fish with more paprika and pepper, place it on the pan, and roast for 6 to 8 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
Finish with lemon and green onion if using and serve hot with the blackened spices on top.

name: Cajun Beef and Peppers
instructions:
Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat and cook the beef with cajun seasoning for 5 to 6 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the bell pepper and onion if using, then cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the peppers soften but still hold their shape.
Stir in the rice and cook over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until hot and lightly coated with the skillet juices.
Finish with green onion and hot sauce if using and serve hot while the peppers still have bite.

name: Southern Sausage Potato Skillet
instructions:
Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat with a splash of oil, then cook the sausage for 4 to 5 minutes until browned and hot through.
Add the potato and onion, cover, and cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the potato starts to soften.
Uncover, add bell pepper if using, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes more until the potatoes are browned and fork-tender.
Finish with green onion and pepper if using, then serve straight from the skillet while hot.

name: Cajun Shrimp and Okra Rice
instructions:
Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat, add the okra, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until it starts to brown at the edges.
Add the shrimp and cajun seasoning, then cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the shrimp are pink, curled, and opaque.
Stir in the rice with tomato sauce and pepper if using, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the rice is hot and coated.
Finish with green onion if using and serve hot while the okra still has texture.

name: BBQ Chicken Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned at the edges and no longer pink in the center.
Stir in the BBQ sauce with corn and cabbage if using, then cook over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce is sticky and hot throughout.
Spoon the BBQ chicken over the rice, finish with green onion if using, and serve while glossy.

name: BBQ Pork Rice Skillet
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat and cook the pork for 5 to 6 minutes until browned at the edges and firm with no pink in the center.
Stir in the BBQ sauce, corn if using, and cooked rice, then cook over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce turns sticky and coats the grains.
Finish with green onion and pepper if using, then serve straight from the skillet while hot.

name: Smoky BBQ Shrimp Tacos
instructions:
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 to 30 seconds per side so they stay flexible.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat, then cook the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes per side until pink, opaque, and curled into loose C-shapes.
Stir in the BBQ sauce and lime if using for 1 minute until the shrimp are glossy and smoky-sweet.
Fill the tortillas with the shrimp, cabbage and green onion if using, and serve right away while the tortillas are soft.

name: BBQ Sausage Potato Sheet Pan
instructions:
Heat the oven to 425F and toss the potatoes with oil, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan.
Roast the potatoes for 15 minutes so they get a head start and begin to brown at the edges.
Add the sausage and green beans, drizzle with the bbq sauce if using, and roast for 12 to 15 minutes more until the sausage is browned and hot in the center and the green beans are crisp-tender.
Rest for 2 minutes, top with green onion if using, and serve when the potatoes are tender.

name: Lemon Herb Salmon Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a skillet over medium heat with the olive oil if using and cook the salmon for 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned, the center reaches 145F, and the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Squeeze in the lemon during the last minute, spoon the pan juices over the salmon, then rest the fish for 1 minute and break it into large pieces.
Build the bowls with the rice, salmon, fresh cucumber, and tomato if using, then finish with parsley and any extra lemon juice so the herb-lemon topping matches the title.

name: Garlic Oregano Shrimp Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat, then cook the shrimp with garlic and oregano for 1 to 2 minutes per side until pink, opaque, and curled into loose C-shapes.
Stir in tomato if using for 1 minute until the pan juices are fragrant and lightly glossy.
Spoon the shrimp over the rice with cucumber, parsley, and olive oil if using, and serve while warm.

name: Lemon Herb Chicken Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned at the edges.
Squeeze in lemon and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until the chicken is no longer pink in the center and the pan juices are bright.
Spoon the chicken over the rice with cucumber, tomato, parsley, and olive oil if using, and serve while warm.

name: Mediterranean Tuna Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a skillet over medium heat with olive oil if using, then warm the tuna for 2 to 3 minutes until hot but not dry.
Fold in cucumber and tomato if using for 1 minute so they stay fresh but take on the warm pan juices.
Spoon the tuna mixture over the rice, finish with parsley if using, and serve while the bowl is warm.

name: Herbed Chickpea Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a skillet over medium heat with olive oil if using, then cook the chickpeas for 4 to 5 minutes until hot and lightly browned.
Fold in cucumber and tomato if using for 1 minute so they stay crisp and fresh.
Spoon the chickpeas over the rice, finish with parsley if using, and serve while the bowl is warm.

name: Tomato Feta Chicken Skillet
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with olive oil if using, then cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Stir in the tomato sauce and rice, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the rice is hot and the sauce clings lightly.
Fold in spinach if using for 1 minute until just wilted, then crumble feta over the top.
Finish with parsley and lemon if using and serve hot while the feta is soft but still distinct.

name: Lemon Herb Salmon Sheet Pan
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and cut the potato into small pieces so it cooks evenly with the salmon.
Toss the potato and green beans with olive oil if using, salt, and pepper, then roast on a sheet pan for 12 minutes.
Add the salmon, season it with lemon and parsley, and roast for 8 to 10 minutes until the salmon flakes easily and the potatoes are tender.
Rest the sheet pan for 2 minutes, then serve hot with the lemon-herb pan juices spooned over the salmon.

name: Lemon Chickpea Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat with olive oil if using, then add the chickpeas and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until lightly toasted at the edges.
Stir in the rice with 4 cups water, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 12 to 14 minutes until the rice is tender.
Add the spinach and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted and bright green.
Finish with lemon juice and parsley if using, then serve hot while the broth is bright and the rice is still distinct.

name: Roasted Veggie Feta Pasta
instructions:
Cook the pasta for 8 to 10 minutes until just tender, then reserve 1/2 cup cooking water and drain.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with olive oil if using, then cook the mushroom and zucchini for 5 to 6 minutes until browned at the edges.
Add tomato if using and cook for 2 minutes until it softens, then toss in the pasta with a splash of reserved water.
Fold in the feta off the heat so it turns creamy in spots but still leaves a few salty crumbles, then serve hot.

name: Zucchini Chickpea Orzo
instructions:
Cook the orzo for 7 to 9 minutes until just tender, then drain it and keep 1/2 cup cooking water.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with olive oil if using, add the zucchini, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until tender and lightly browned.
Add the chickpeas and orzo with a splash of cooking water, then cook over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until glossy and hot.
Fold in feta and parsley if using and serve while the zucchini still has texture.

name: Greek Stuffed Peppers
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and lightly oil a baking dish.
Cook or warm the rice, then mix it with chickpeas, parsley, and olive oil if using for 2 minutes until evenly seasoned.
Spoon the chickpea-rice mixture into the bell peppers and bake for 22 to 26 minutes until the peppers are tender and lightly browned at the edges.
Crumble feta over the top if using, return to the oven for 3 to 4 minutes until softened, and serve warm.

name: Mediterranean Shrimp Rice Bake
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and lightly oil a baking dish.
Spread the rice and tomato in the dish with a splash of water or broth, then bake for 10 minutes until the tomato juices start to bubble.
Add the shrimp and bake for 8 to 10 minutes more until they are pink, opaque, and curled into loose C-shapes.
Rest for 3 minutes, then finish with olives, parsley, and lemon if using before serving warm.

name: Coconut Shrimp Curry
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a pot over medium heat with a splash of oil, then cook the onion if using for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink, opaque, and curled, then brighten with lime or yogurt if using and serve over the rice.

name: Coconut Salmon Curry
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a pot over medium heat with a splash of oil, then cook the onion if using for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Add the salmon and simmer gently for 5 to 7 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, then brighten with lime or yogurt if using and serve over the rice.

name: Ginger Garlic Chicken Curry
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a deep skillet or pot over medium heat and cook the onion if using with the ginger, garlic, and curry powder for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Add the chicken and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until it loses its raw color and starts to brown in spots.
Stir in the tomato sauce with a splash of water and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked and the sauce thickens into a rich curry.
Taste and brighten with lime or yogurt if using, then spoon the curry over rice and finish with cilantro if using.

name: Tomato Cod Curry
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a pot over medium heat with a splash of oil, then cook the onion if using for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the tomato sauce and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until it darkens slightly and tastes savory.
Add the cod and simmer gently for 5 to 7 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, then brighten with lime or yogurt if using and serve over the rice.

name: Turmeric Salmon Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat, then cook the salmon for 3 to 4 minutes on the first side until browned.
Flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more with turmeric-style seasoning until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Fold in the spinach for 1 minute until wilted, then spoon the salmon and spinach over the rice with cilantro, lime, or yogurt if using.

name: Ginger Chicken Lentil Skillet
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a splash of oil, then cook the chicken and ginger for 5 to 6 minutes until browned at the edges.
Stir in the lentils with a splash of water, lower the heat to medium, and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until the lentils are hot and the chicken is no longer pink in the center.
Fold in the spinach for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted and glossy.
Serve straight from the skillet or spoon it over rice with cilantro, lime, or yogurt if using.

name: Potato Pea Curry
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a pot over medium heat with a splash of oil, then cook the potato for 5 to 6 minutes until the edges begin to soften.
Add enough water to barely cover, then simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until the potato is tender and the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in the peas for 2 minutes until hot, then brighten with cilantro, lime, or yogurt if using and serve over the rice.

name: Garlic Spinach Lentil Curry
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender.
Heat a pot over medium heat with a splash of oil, then cook the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lentils with enough water to loosen them and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until hot and lightly thickened.
Fold in the spinach for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted, then brighten with cilantro, lime, or yogurt if using and serve over the rice.

name: Tomato Lentil Spinach Stew
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat, add the lentils and tomato sauce, and cook for 2 minutes until the sauce darkens slightly.
Stir in 4 cups water, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 16 to 18 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Add the spinach and rice if using, then simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the spinach wilts and the stew thickens lightly.
Finish with cilantro and lime if using and serve hot while the lentils are soft but not broken down.

name: Chicken Coconut Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium-high heat, add the chicken and onion if using, and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until the chicken is browned and cooked through.
Stir in the coconut milk with 2 cups water and the rice, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until the rice is tender.
Add the spinach and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted.
Finish with cilantro and lime if using and serve hot while the coconut broth is creamy.

name: Turmeric Fish Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat, add onion if using, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the turmeric and rice with 4 cups water, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until the rice is nearly tender.
Add the white fish and simmer gently for 4 to 5 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
Stir in the spinach for 1 minute until wilted, then finish with cilantro and lime if using and serve hot.

name: Pesto Salmon Pasta
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until just shy of tender while you heat a skillet with a little oil over medium-high heat. Add the salmon and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side until it flakes easily. Lower the heat to medium and toss the hot pasta with the pesto so the noodles are evenly coated, then fold in the salmon and spinach if using just until the greens wilt. Finish with parmesan and lemon if you like, and serve while the pasta is glossy and hot.

name: Chicken Mozzarella Bake
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and cook the pasta for 8 to 10 minutes until just shy of tender so it can finish in the sauce.
Spread the pasta and tomato sauce in a baking dish, then nestle the chicken breast into the sauce so it stays covered.
Top with mozzarella and parmesan if using, then bake for 22 to 26 minutes until the chicken reaches 165F and the cheese is browned in spots.
Rest the bake for 5 minutes, finish with parsley if using, and serve within 1 to 2 minutes while the sauce still coats the pasta.

name: Meatball Pepper Bake
instructions:
Heat the oven to 400F and cook the pasta for 8 to 10 minutes until just shy of tender so it can finish in the bake.
Spread the pasta and tomato sauce in a baking dish, then nestle the meatballs and sliced peppers if using into the sauce.
Top with mozzarella and parmesan if using, then bake for 20 to 24 minutes until the meatballs are hot through and the sauce bubbles at the edges.
Rest for 5 minutes, finish with parsley if using, and serve within 1 to 2 minutes while the pasta is tender and coated.

name: Italian Sausage Rice Skillet
instructions: Start the rice first so it is ready when the sausage finishes. Heat a large skillet over medium heat and cook the sausage for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into bite-size pieces, until browned and fully cooked. Spoon off excess fat if needed, add a splash of water to loosen the browned bits, then stir in the cooked rice and spinach and cook for 2 minutes until the spinach wilts into the rice. Turn off the heat, fold in parmesan if using, and finish with parsley or basil so the skillet stays savory and bright.

name: Garlic Shrimp Tomato Rice Skillet
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the shrimp and garlic, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the shrimp are pink, curled, and opaque.
Move the shrimp to a plate, then stir tomato sauce and rice into the skillet over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes until the rice is hot and coated.
Fold in spinach if using for 1 minute until wilted, then return the shrimp to warm through.
Finish with parmesan, parsley, or basil if using and serve hot while the tomato sauce is glossy.

name: Tuscan White Bean Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat with olive oil if using, add the white beans, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the beans are hot and lightly creamy at the edges.
Stir in the rice with 4 cups water, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 12 to 14 minutes until the rice is tender.
Add the spinach and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted.
Finish with parmesan and parsley if using and serve hot while the beans make the broth lightly creamy.

name: Chicken Orzo Soup
instructions: Heat a soup pot over medium heat and cook the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until it loses its raw color and starts to firm up. Add enough broth or water to make a soupy base, bring it to a boil, stir in the orzo, and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the orzo is tender and the chicken is fully cooked. Stir in the spinach for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted, then finish with parmesan, parsley, and lemon if using and serve hot.

name: Lemon Pepper Salmon Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat until tender while you season the salmon with salt and plenty of black pepper. Heat a skillet over medium heat with a little oil and cook the salmon for 3 to 4 minutes per side until it flakes easily and is opaque through the center. Transfer it to a plate to rest.
Add the green beans to the same skillet with a splash of water and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp-tender. Stir in the butter and garlic if using, then squeeze in the lemon juice and let it bubble for 30 seconds so the pan tastes bright and peppery.
Break the salmon into large pieces and fold it back into the lemon-pepper pan juices for 30 seconds before spooning it over the rice with the green beans. Finish with parsley if using and serve while the fish still flakes easily.

name: Garlic Herb Tilapia Rice Bowls
instructions:
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until tender, then keep it covered for serving.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat, then cook the tilapia for 3 to 4 minutes on the first side until lightly browned.
Flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more with the green beans and garlic if using until the fish is opaque and flakes easily and the beans are crisp-tender.
Spoon the tilapia and green beans over the rice, finish with parsley, pepper, and lemon if using, and serve within 1 to 2 minutes while the pan juices are warm.

name: Salmon Broccoli Sheet Pan
instructions:
Heat the oven to 425F and toss the potatoes with oil, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan.
Roast the potatoes for 15 minutes so they get a head start and begin to brown at the edges.
Add the broccoli and salmon, dot the salmon with butter and pepper if using, and roast for 10 to 12 minutes more.
Serve hot when the potatoes are tender, the broccoli is browned at the edges, and the salmon flakes easily in the center, with parsley if using.

name: Beef Mushroom Skillet
instructions: Heat a large deep skillet over medium-high heat with the butter or a splash of oil. Add the beef and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, breaking it up or turning it as needed, until it is well browned and cooked through. Stir in the mushrooms and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until they release their moisture and start to brown at the edges; season with pepper if using. Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add 4 cups of water and bring the skillet to a boil. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 16 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Rest for 5 minutes, fold in parsley if using, and serve hot.

name: Chicken Mushroom Gravy Skillet
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes until browned on both sides, then transfer it to a plate. Lower the heat to medium and cook the mushrooms for 5 minutes until they release their liquid and start to brown. Stir in the rice with 2 cups broth or water, scrape up any browned bits, and bring the skillet to a boil. Return the chicken, cover, and simmer on low for 15 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165F in the thickest piece. Stir in the butter and parsley if using, let the skillet stand uncovered for 2 minutes so the pan juices thicken lightly, then serve hot.

name: Creamy White Bean Chicken Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat and cook the onion with the garlic for 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant and softened.
Add the chicken, white beans, and broth if using, bring the pot to a simmer, and cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the beans start to soften into the soup.
Stir in the spinach and milk if using, then simmer gently for 2 to 3 minutes until the spinach wilts and the broth turns creamy without boiling hard.
Taste for salt or acid at the end and ladle the soup while it is still hot enough to steam.

name: Lemon Shrimp White Bean Skillet
instructions: Sear the shrimp in olive oil over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 minutes per side until pink, opaque, and lightly golden before transferring them to a plate. Simmer the white beans with a splash of water for 2 minutes. Fold in the spinach and cook for 1 minute until wilted. Return the shrimp and toss with lemon juice and parsley if using for 30 seconds until warmed through.

name: Tofu Spinach Curry Skillet
instructions:
Brown the tofu in a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, turning every 1 to 2 minutes, until the edges are golden and the center is hot.
Stir in the curry seasoning and a splash of water over medium heat for 30 seconds, then fold in the spinach for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted and the tofu is evenly coated.
Warm the rice for 1 to 2 minutes, spoon on the tofu and spinach, and top with cilantro, lime, or yogurt if using.

name: Lentil Coconut Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium heat, add the lentils and coconut milk with 3 cups water, and bring to a gentle boil.
Reduce to medium-low and simmer for 16 to 18 minutes until the lentils are tender and the coconut broth thickens lightly.
Stir in the rice and spinach, then cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the rice is hot and the spinach wilts.
Finish with cilantro and lime if using and serve hot while the coconut broth is creamy.

name: Chicken Pesto Rice Skillet
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned in spots and cooked through with no pink remaining.
Stir in the rice and the amount of water called for on the package, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fold in the pesto and spinach if using and cook for 1 minute until the spinach wilts and the rice is evenly coated.
Finish with parmesan and parsley if using, then serve hot.

name: White Bean Sausage Soup
instructions:
Heat a soup pot over medium-high heat and cook the sausage for 5 to 6 minutes until browned at the edges.
Add the white beans and tomato sauce if using, then stir for 2 minutes until the beans are hot and lightly coated.
Add 4 cups water, reduce the heat to medium, and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the sausage flavors the broth.
Stir in the spinach for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted, then finish with parmesan and parsley if using and serve hot.
